title: Lamentation (The Mourning of Christ)
note: Part of the Scrovegni Chapel cycle; grieving figures and a diagonal rock ledge carry real emotional weight.
image_file: Compianto sul Cristo morto.jpg
description: This scene belongs to the cycle of frescoes Giotto painted around 1305 for the Scrovegni Chapel in Padua. The chapel was commissioned by the banker Enrico Scrovegni, partly in atonement for his father's notorious usury. The dead Christ lies in his mother's arms at the lower left, and a bare rocky ridge runs diagonally down towards him, leading the eye to the focus of grief. Mourners crowd around, two of them seen from behind as anonymous solid masses, a daring new idea. Above, angels twist and wail in the sky. Each figure expresses sorrow differently, from John flinging his arms back to Mary Magdalene cradling Christ's feet. The scene has the force of real human drama, a decisive break from the stylised Byzantine tradition.
creator: giotto

title: Ognissanti Madonna
note: The enthroned Virgin has a solid, three-dimensional body unlike earlier Byzantine-style Madonnas.
image_file: Giotto, 1267 Around-1337 - Maestà - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted around 1310 for the church of the Ognissanti (All Saints) in Florence, this altarpiece more than three metres tall shows the Virgin enthroned with the Child, surrounded by saints and angels. Compared with Cimabue's and Duccio's Madonnas, Giotto's Virgin has a weighty, three-dimensional body: her knees and breast press against her robes, and she sits firmly in a Gothic throne that recedes into space. Kneeling angels offer flowers, and the saints behind them overlap convincingly. It was a landmark in giving sacred figures physical presence.
creator: giotto

title: David
note: The first free-standing nude male statue made since antiquity.
image_file: Donatello, David, bronze, 1435-40, Florence, Bargello, detail.jpg
description: Donatello's bronze David is the first free-standing life-size nude statue made in Europe since antiquity. Its date is debated, usually placed between the 1430s and the 1450s. It was made for the Medici, probably to stand in the courtyard of their palace. The slender young hero wears only a wide-brimmed shepherd's hat and boots, and he rests one foot on the severed head of Goliath, his sword at his side. His relaxed contrapposto stance, soft adolescent body and dreamy expression have prompted endless discussion of its meaning, from a symbol of Florence's freedom to an expression of sensual beauty. When the Medici were expelled in 1495 the statue was moved to the Palazzo della Signoria as a civic emblem.
creator: donatello

title: Primavera
note: A mythological allegory of spring set in an orange grove, with Venus at its centre.
image_file: Botticelli-primavera.jpg
description: Primavera ('Spring'), painted around 1480 for a member of the Medici family, is set in an orange grove on a flowery meadow where botanists have identified hundreds of plants. Venus stands at the centre with blindfolded Cupid aiming an arrow above her. At right, the blue wind god Zephyrus seizes the nymph Chloris, who turns into Flora, goddess of spring, scattering flowers. At left, the Three Graces dance in transparent veils, and Mercury raises his staff to disperse clouds. The painting probably celebrates love and marriage in Neoplatonic terms, though its exact meaning is still argued over. It hung in a Medici town house before entering the Uffizi.
creator: botticelli

title: The Birth of Venus
note: Venus arrives on a shell, blown ashore by the winds; a landmark of mythological painting.
image_file: Sandro Botticelli - La nascita di Venere - Google Art Project - edited.jpg
description: Probably painted in the mid-1480s, this large canvas shows Venus, goddess of love, arriving at the shore of Cyprus on a scallop shell after her birth from the sea. At left, the wind god Zephyrus and a female companion blow her ashore amid falling roses, and at right a Hora (goddess of the seasons) rushes to cover her with a flowered cloak. Venus's pose, covering herself with her hand and hair, is borrowed from ancient statues of the modest Venus, but her elongated neck and sloping shoulders are pure Botticelli. It was one of the first large paintings on canvas in Florence and one of the first since antiquity to show a mythological nude on such a scale.
creator: botticelli

title: Ghent Altarpiece (Adoration of the Mystic Lamb)
note: Begun with his brother Hubert; one of the most stolen and studied artworks in history.
image_file: Ghent Altarpiece Google Art Project.jpg
description: This huge folding altarpiece was commissioned by the Ghent merchant Joos Vijd and his wife Elisabeth Borluut for their chapel in what is now St Bavo's Cathedral. An inscription says it was begun by Hubert van Eyck and completed by his brother Jan in 1432. When open, the upper register shows God enthroned between the Virgin and John the Baptist, flanked by singing angels and the strikingly realistic nude figures of Adam and Eve. Below, crowds of saints, prophets and martyrs converge on a meadow to adore the Lamb of God on an altar. It has been called the most stolen artwork in history: looted by Napoleon's troops, sold off in parts, and hidden by the Nazis in an Austrian salt mine. One panel, the Just Judges, was stolen in 1934 and has never been recovered. A restoration begun in 2012 removed later overpaint and revealed the Lamb's startlingly human original face.
creator: van-eyck

title: Arnolfini Portrait
note: A convex mirror reflects the room and two figures; the painter's signature reads 'Jan van Eyck was here'.
image_file: The Arnolfini portrait (1434).jpg
description: Dated 1434, this small oak panel shows a wealthy Italian merchant, usually identified as Giovanni di Nicolao Arnolfini, and a woman, standing in a room of their house in Bruges. Every detail is rendered with astonishing precision: the dog, the oranges on the sill, the brass chandelier with a single lit candle, the discarded clogs. A convex mirror on the back wall reflects the couple from behind and two more figures in the doorway. Above it Van Eyck wrote in elaborate script, 'Johannes de eyck fuit hic 1434' ('Jan van Eyck was here'). It was long read as a wedding contract with the painter as witness. Scholars now debate whether it records a betrothal, celebrates a marriage, or even commemorates a dead wife. The National Gallery in London bought it in 1842.
creator: van-eyck

title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
note: Paradise, a dreamlike garden of pleasures and a nightmarish hell across three panels.
image_file: The Garden of earthly delights.jpg
description: Painted around 1490–1510, probably for the Nassau family's palace in Brussels, this triptych shows the world's history from creation to damnation. Closed, its shutters show the world on the third day of creation, painted in grey tones inside a crystal sphere. Open, the left panel shows God presenting Eve to Adam in Eden. The vast central panel is a paradise of naked men and women frolicking with giant birds, oversized fruit and fantastic structures, perhaps humanity lost in sensual pleasure. The right panel is a nightmarish hell where sinners are tortured with giant musical instruments, gamblers are punished, and a pale 'Tree-Man' gazes out from among the flames. Philip II acquired it in 1593, and it is now the most famous work in the Prado.
creator: bosch

title: Self-Portrait at Twenty-Eight
note: A frontal, Christ-like self-portrait asserting the artist's dignity.
image_file: Dürer Alte Pinakothek.jpg
description: In 1500, a year many expected to bring the end of the world, Dürer painted himself in strict frontal view. Such symmetry was normally reserved for images of Christ. His long curled hair frames his face, and his hand touches the fur collar of his coat in a gesture recalling a blessing. The Latin inscription reads: 'I, Albrecht Dürer of Nuremberg, painted myself thus, with undying colours, at the age of 28 years.' The painting is not blasphemous. It asserts that the artist's creative gift comes from God and gives the painter a dignity once reserved for scholars and princes. It is in the Alte Pinakothek, Munich.
creator: durer

title: Young Hare
note: A celebrated study of nature in minute detail.
image_file: Albrecht Dürer - Hare, 1502 - Google Art Project.jpg
description: This watercolour and gouache study of 1502, in the Albertina in Vienna, is one of the most famous nature studies ever made. The hare crouches, ears alert, and every hair is built up with fine strokes of brush, from the soft underbelly to the stiff whiskers. Look closely and you can see a window reflected in the animal's eye, suggesting it was studied indoors. Dürer probably worked from a live or dead hare together with sketches, combining close observation with studio skill. Studies like this fed into the animals in his prints and paintings.
creator: durer

title: Melencolia I
note: An enigmatic allegory of melancholy and creative genius, crowded with symbols.
image_file: Albrecht Dürer - Melencolia I - Google Art Project ( AGDdr3EHmNGyA).jpg
description: One of Dürer's three 'Master Engravings' of 1513–14, Melencolia I shows a brooding winged figure seated amid scattered tools: a compass, plane, saw, nails, a large polyhedron, a sphere, an hourglass, scales, a bell and a ladder. A starved dog sleeps at her feet and a comet blazes over the sea. On the wall is a 'magic square' whose rows, columns and diagonals all add up to 34, with the date 1514 in the bottom row. The print draws on Renaissance ideas that melancholy, one of the four temperaments, was the condition of creative genius and also of paralysing doubt. It has been interpreted endlessly and is one of the most discussed images in Western art.
creator: durer

title: The Tower of Babel
note: The biblical tower modelled on the Roman Colosseum.
image_file: Pieter Bruegel the Elder - The Tower of Babel (Vienna) - Google Art Project - edited.jpg
description: Bruegel painted the Tower of Babel at least three times. This large panel of 1563 is in Vienna, and a smaller version is in Rotterdam. The biblical tower, built by humans trying to reach heaven, rises in tiers inspired by the Roman Colosseum, which Bruegel had seen in Rome. It is already crumbling and leaning even as construction continues. Hundreds of tiny workers, cranes, scaffolds and ships at the harbour are shown in meticulous detail. In the foreground, King Nimrod visits the stonemasons, who kneel before him. In a busy commercial city like Antwerp, the painting could be read as a warning against pride and ambition and perhaps a comment on the city's many languages.
creator: bruegel

title: The Hunters in the Snow
note: One of a series of the months; weary hunters return to a frozen village.
image_file: Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Hunters in the Snow (Winter) - Google Art Project.jpg
description: This 1565 painting belongs to a series of six showing the times of the year, made for the Antwerp merchant Nicolaes Jongelinck. Five survive, three of them in Vienna. Weary hunters trudge back to their village with their hounds and only a single fox to show for their efforts. A sign hangs askew outside an inn where peasants are singeing a pig over a fire. Below, villagers skate and play on frozen ponds, and the landscape stretches out to jagged Alpine peaks under a cold greenish sky. Crows perch on bare trees. The painting captures the mood of a whole season, and it was painted during one of the harshest winters of the 'Little Ice Age'.
creator: bruegel

title: Lady with an Ermine
note: Portrait of Cecilia Gallerani with a turning, lively pose.
image_file: Lady with an Ermine - Leonardo da Vinci (adjusted levels).jpg
description: Painted around 1489–91 in Milan, this portrait shows Cecilia Gallerani, the teenage mistress of Duke Ludovico Sforza. She turns her head and body in opposite directions as if responding to someone outside the picture, a dynamic pose new to portraiture. She holds an ermine, a symbol of purity, which also puns on her name (the Greek for ermine is 'galê') and refers to Ludovico, who belonged to the Order of the Ermine. Her elegant hand and the animal's lithe body echo each other. The painting was bought by the Polish Czartoryski family around 1800, seized by the Nazis during the Second World War and recovered in 1946. It is now in the National Museum in Kraków.
creator: leonardo

title: The Last Supper
note: Captures the moment Jesus announces his betrayal; Leonardo's experimental technique began to flake within his lifetime.
image_file: The Last Supper - Leonardo Da Vinci - High Resolution 32x16.jpg
description: Leonardo painted the Last Supper around 1495–98 on the end wall of the refectory of the Dominican convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan, for Ludovico Sforza. It captures the instant after Jesus says 'One of you will betray me.' The apostles react in four groups of three, with waves of shock, denial and questioning moving out from the calm central figure of Christ. All the lines of the perspective converge on his head. Leonardo rejected traditional fresco and painted with tempera and oil on dry plaster so he could work slowly, but the paint began to flake within his lifetime. The mural survived a 1943 bombing that destroyed much of the refectory and was restored over more than 20 years, finishing in 1999.
creator: leonardo

title: Mona Lisa
note: The most famous painting in the world, a showcase of sfumato and ambiguous expression.
image_file: Mona Lisa, by Leonardo da Vinci, from C2RMF retouched.jpg
description: Leonardo began this portrait around 1503 of Lisa Gherardini, wife of the Florentine silk merchant Francesco del Giocondo, which is why it is also called La Gioconda. He never delivered it, kept working on it for years and took it to France, where it entered the royal collection of Francis I. The sitter's famously elusive smile, the soft sfumato shading around her eyes and mouth, her calm folded hands and the hazy imaginary landscape behind her made the painting a model for portraiture. It became world-famous after it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 by the Italian handyman Vincenzo Peruggia. It was recovered in Florence in 1913, and today millions of visitors see it each year behind protective glass.
creator: leonardo

title: Pietà
note: The only work Michelangelo signed, carved in his early twenties.
image_file: Pieta de Michelangelo - Vaticano.jpg
description: The French cardinal Jean de Bilhères commissioned this marble Pietà, the Virgin mourning the dead Christ on her lap, for his tomb. Michelangelo carved it in 1498–99, when he was in his early twenties. He solved the problem of holding an adult man on a woman's lap by making Mary's body larger and her robes deep and voluminous. He gave her a young, serene face, explaining, according to his biographer Condivi, that purity preserves youth. It is the only work Michelangelo ever signed: his name is carved across the strap on Mary's breast, reportedly after he heard others credited for it. In 1972 a man attacked it with a hammer, and after restoration it has been shown behind glass in St Peter's Basilica.
creator: michelangelo

title: David
note: Over 5 m tall, a symbol of the Florentine Republic, shown before his fight with Goliath.
image_file: 'David' by Michelangelo Fir JBU004.jpg
description: In 1501 the cathedral works in Florence gave the 26-year-old Michelangelo a huge, narrow block of marble that earlier sculptors had begun and abandoned. By 1504 he had carved from it a David over 5 metres tall. Instead of showing the hero triumphant over Goliath's head, he chose the tense moment before the fight. David stands in relaxed contrapposto with his sling over his shoulder, but his brow is furrowed and his gaze fixed on the enemy. The oversized head and hands make him read clearly from below. A committee of artists, including Leonardo and Botticelli, decided to place it outside the Palazzo della Signoria as a symbol of the Florentine Republic's defiance of tyranny. It was moved indoors to the Accademia in 1873, and a copy now stands in its place.
creator: michelangelo

title: Sistine Chapel Ceiling
note: Scenes from Genesis including The Creation of Adam, painted for Pope Julius II.
image_file: Sistine Chapel ceiling 02 (brightened).jpg
description: Pope Julius II persuaded a reluctant Michelangelo, who considered himself a sculptor, to paint the ceiling of the papal chapel. Between 1508 and 1512, working on scaffolding he designed himself, he covered some 500 square metres with more than 300 figures. Down the centre run nine scenes from Genesis, from the Separation of Light and Darkness to the Drunkenness of Noah, including the Creation of Adam, in which God's finger reaches towards Adam's. Around them sit monumental prophets and sibyls, the ancestors of Christ, and the energetic nude youths called ignudi. Contrary to legend, he painted standing and bending backwards rather than lying down. A restoration completed in 1994 removed centuries of grime and revealed brilliant colours.
creator: michelangelo

title: The Last Judgment
note: A swirling altar-wall vision of the end of time; its nudes were later partly covered.
image_file: Last Judgement (Michelangelo).jpg
description: More than twenty years after the ceiling, Michelangelo returned to the Sistine Chapel to paint the entire altar wall (1536–41) for Pope Paul III. A powerful, beardless Christ raises his arm in judgement at the centre of a swirling vortex of more than 300 figures. The saved rise towards heaven on the left, and the damned are dragged down to hell on the right, where Charon beats them from his boat. St Bartholomew holds his own flayed skin, whose sagging face is generally read as Michelangelo's self-portrait. The many nudes provoked fierce criticism, and after his death the painter Daniele da Volterra was hired to paint drapery over the genitals, earning the nickname 'Il Braghettone' ('the breeches-maker').
creator: michelangelo

title: The School of Athens
location: Stanza della Segnatura, Apostolic Palace, Vatican City
note: Plato and Aristotle at the centre of a gathering of ancient philosophers in ideal architecture.
image_file: "The School of Athens" by Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino.jpg
description: Painted in 1509–11 in the Stanza della Segnatura, probably Julius II's library, this fresco celebrates philosophy and faces Raphael's Disputation of the Holy Sacrament, which celebrates theology. Under vast coffered vaults inspired by Bramante's designs for St Peter's, the greatest thinkers of antiquity gather. At the centre Plato, with Leonardo's features, points upward to the realm of ideas, while Aristotle gestures towards the earth. Around them are Socrates, Pythagoras, Euclid with a compass (probably given Bramante's face) and Diogenes sprawled on the steps. The brooding figure of Heraclitus in front is thought to portray Michelangelo, who was painting the Sistine ceiling nearby. Raphael included his own portrait looking out at the far right.
creator: raphael

title: Sistine Madonna
note: Famous for the two bored cherubs at the bottom edge.
image_file: RAFAEL - Madonna Sixtina (Gemäldegalerie Alter Meister, Dresden, 1513-14. Óleo sobre lienzo, 265 x 196 cm).jpg
description: Raphael painted this altarpiece in 1512–13 for the Benedictine church of San Sisto in Piacenza. The Virgin, carrying the Christ Child, walks forward on clouds as green curtains are drawn back, flanked by St Sixtus and St Barbara. Below, two winged cherubs lean on the ledge looking up dreamily. They have become some of the most reproduced images in the world, appearing on everything from postcards to stamps. Augustus III, King of Poland and Elector of Saxony, bought the painting in 1754 for Dresden. Soviet troops took it to Moscow in 1945, and it was returned to Dresden in 1955.
creator: raphael

title: Assumption of the Virgin
note: A huge altarpiece that established Titian as Venice's leading painter.
image_file: Tizian 041.jpg
description: This enormous altarpiece, nearly 7 metres high, was installed on the high altar of the Franciscan church of Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari in Venice in 1518. It shows the Virgin Mary carried up to heaven. Below, the apostles reach up in amazement. In the middle, Mary rises on a cloud, borne by a swirl of cherubs, her red robe glowing. Above, God the Father leans down to receive her in a golden sky. The bold scale, energetic movement and blazing colour were unprecedented in Venice, and the picture announced Titian as the city's leading painter. It is still in place in the church for which it was made.
creator: titian

title: Venus of Urbino
note: A reclining nude that became the model for Manet's Olympia.
image_file: Tiziano - Venere di Urbino - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted in 1538 and bought by Guidobaldo della Rovere, soon to be Duke of Urbino, this canvas shows a nude woman reclining on a white sheet, looking directly at the viewer with a small bouquet of roses in her hand. A little dog sleeps at her feet. In the background, two maids search a chest (cassone) for clothes. The painting has been read as a celebration of married love, with the dog symbolising fidelity and the chests a bride's trousseau, and also as a frankly sensual image for private pleasure. It transformed Giorgione's sleeping Venus into a wakeful, knowing woman, and it later inspired Manet's Olympia. It is in the Uffizi.
creator: titian

title: The Burial of the Count of Orgaz
note: Earthly funeral below, heavenly reception above.
image_file: El Greco - The Burial of the Count of Orgaz.JPG
description: Commissioned in 1586 for the parish church of Santo Tomé in Toledo, where it still hangs, this painting illustrates a local legend. At the burial of the pious nobleman Don Gonzalo Ruiz, lord of Orgaz, in 1323, St Stephen and St Augustine came down from heaven to lay him in his tomb with their own hands. In the lower half, the saints in gold vestments lower the armoured body before a row of solemn Toledan gentlemen dressed in the black of the 1580s, many of them probably real portraits. A boy at left points to the scene; he is thought to be El Greco's son, Jorge Manuel, and the handkerchief in his pocket bears the year of his birth, 1578. Above, the count's soul is carried up to Christ, the Virgin and the saints in a swirling, luminous heaven.
creator: el-greco

title: View of Toledo
location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: A stormy, visionary landscape of his adopted city.
image_file: El Greco View of Toledo.jpg
description: One of only two surviving landscapes by El Greco, this painting of around 1596–1600 shows his adopted city under a stormy sky of churning blue-black clouds. Toledo spreads over its hill above the River Tagus, its buildings glowing an eerie silver-green. El Greco took liberties: he moved the cathedral bell tower to sit beside the Alcázar for dramatic effect. The scene is less a topographical record than a spiritual vision of the city, and its expressive distortion and colour made it an icon for modern painters. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
creator: el-greco

title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
location: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica (Palazzo Barberini), Rome
note: A shockingly direct depiction of the biblical beheading.
image_file: Caravaggio - Giuditta e Oloferne (ca. 1599).jpg
description: Painted around 1598–99 and now in the Palazzo Barberini in Rome, this canvas shows the Old Testament heroine Judith killing the Assyrian general Holofernes to save her people. Caravaggio shows the gruesome moment itself: Holofernes screams and twists on his bed as Judith saws through his neck with his own sword and blood spurts across the sheets. Judith holds herself at arm's length with a frown of concentration and distaste, and her old maid stands by eagerly holding the bag for the head. The strong light from the left, the deep black background and the red curtain intensify the drama. The model for Judith is thought to be the Roman courtesan Fillide Melandroni.
creator: caravaggio

title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
location: Contarelli Chapel, San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome
note: A beam of light follows Christ's pointing hand into a tavern-like counting room.
image_file: Caravaggio — The Calling of Saint Matthew.jpg
description: This was one of a pair of large canvases that made Caravaggio famous when they were unveiled in 1600 in the Contarelli Chapel of San Luigi dei Francesi, the French national church in Rome, where they still hang. Christ, almost hidden behind St Peter, enters a dim counting room and points at the tax collector Levi, who will become the apostle Matthew. His gesture echoes God's hand in Michelangelo's Creation of Adam. A shaft of light enters from the upper right, following the direction of the real window in the chapel, and falls on the faces of men in contemporary clothes counting money at a table. Scholars still debate whether Matthew is the bearded man pointing to himself, as if asking 'Me?', or the young man hunched over coins at the end of the table.
creator: caravaggio

title: Judith Slaying Holofernes
note: Her best-known version of the subject, more physically forceful than Caravaggio's.
image_file: Artemisia Gentileschi - Judith Beheading Holofernes - WGA8563.jpg
description: Artemisia painted the story of Judith and Holofernes several times. This version of around 1620, in the Uffizi, was made for the Medici court in Florence and is a reworking of an earlier version now in Naples. Unlike Caravaggio's hesitant Judith, Artemisia's heroine and her maid Abra work together with grim physical determination: the maid pins Holofernes down while Judith braces herself and drives the sword through his neck, and blood spurts in arcs across the white sheets. A bracelet on Judith's arm shows images of the huntress goddess Artemis, perhaps a reference to the painter's own name. Many viewers have read the painting in the light of her own experience of rape and trial, but it is above all a masterpiece of Baroque drama and physical realism.
creator: artemisia

title: The Elevation of the Cross
note: Straining bodies heave the cross upright in a powerful diagonal.
image_file: Peter Paul Rubens - Raising of the Cross (Antwerp Cathedral).JPG
description: Rubens painted this huge triptych in 1610–11, soon after returning from Italy, for the high altar of the church of St Walburga in Antwerp. It was moved to the Cathedral of Our Lady in 1816, after being taken to Paris under Napoleon and returned. Across all three panels, muscular men strain to haul the cross with Christ upright along a dramatic diagonal. In the side wings, mourners grieve at left and Roman officers watch at right. The heroic bodies show what Rubens learned from Michelangelo's nudes and Hellenistic sculpture, and the dramatic light owes something to Caravaggio. With his Descent from the Cross in the same cathedral, it established him as the leading painter of the Southern Netherlands.
creator: rubens

title: Apollo and Daphne
note: Daphne turns into a laurel tree at the moment Apollo catches her.
image_file: Apollo and Daphne (Bernini) (cropped).jpg
description: Carved in 1622–25 for Cardinal Scipione Borghese, this life-size marble group, which remains in the Galleria Borghese, illustrates a story from Ovid's Metamorphoses. The god Apollo, struck by Cupid's arrow, chases the nymph Daphne, who prays to her father, a river god, to save her. At the very moment Apollo touches her, she turns into a laurel tree: bark encloses her legs, her toes become roots, and leaves sprout from her fingers and streaming hair. Bernini, working with his assistant Giuliano Finelli on the delicate leaves, made hard marble look like moving flesh and fluttering foliage. Cardinal Maffeo Barberini, later Pope Urban VIII, wrote a moralising Latin couplet for the base to make the pagan love story acceptable.
creator: bernini

title: Ecstasy of Saint Teresa
location: Cornaro Chapel, Santa Maria della Vittoria, Rome
note: Sculpture, architecture and hidden light combine into one theatrical whole.
image_file: Ecstasy of St. Teresa HDR.jpg
description: Made in 1647–52 for the Cornaro Chapel in the church of Santa Maria della Vittoria in Rome, commissioned by the Venetian cardinal Federico Cornaro, this ensemble stages a vision described by the Spanish mystic Teresa of Ávila. An angel pierced her heart with a golden spear, leaving her 'on fire with a great love of God'. Teresa swoons on a cloud, her eyes half closed and her lips parted, while the smiling angel prepares to strike again. Natural light from a hidden window above falls down gilded bronze rays. On the side walls, members of the Cornaro family sit in theatre boxes as if watching the scene. The combination of sculpture, architecture, coloured marble and light is the supreme example of Bernini's theatrical Baroque.
creator: bernini

title: The Night Watch
note: A civic militia portrait turned into a dramatic scene of movement and light.
image_file: La ronda de noche, por Rembrandt van Rijn.jpg
description: Officially titled Militia Company of District II under the Command of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq, this huge canvas of 1642 was commissioned to hang in the hall of Amsterdam's arquebusiers' guild. Instead of the usual rows of portraits, Rembrandt showed the company bursting into action as the captain, in black with a red sash, orders his lieutenant in pale yellow to march them out. Around them, muskets are loaded and fired, a drum beats, and a mysterious girl in gold carries a chicken, the company's emblem. The popular name came later, when darkened varnish made the daylight scene look nocturnal. In 1715 the painting was cut down on all sides to fit a wall in the town hall. It has survived three vandal attacks, and since 2019 the Rijksmuseum's Operation Night Watch has studied and restored it in public view.
creator: rembrandt

title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
note: A late masterpiece of forgiveness and tenderness.
image_file: Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn - Return of the Prodigal Son - Google Art Project.jpg
description: This late painting, probably from around 1668, in the Hermitage in St Petersburg, illustrates Jesus's parable of the son who squanders his inheritance and returns home in disgrace, only to be welcomed with love by his father. The ragged son kneels with his shaven head buried against his father's chest, one sandal falling from his worn foot. The old, almost blind father bends over him and lays both hands on his back. Viewers have often noted that one hand looks larger and masculine and the other more slender. At the right, the stern elder brother watches, and other figures emerge from the deep warm shadows. It is one of the most moving images of forgiveness in art.
creator: rembrandt

title: Las Meninas
note: The Infanta Margarita and her attendants, with the painter himself and the king and queen reflected in a mirror.
image_file: Las Meninas, by Diego Velázquez, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg
description: This large painting of 1656, in the Prado, is one of the most analysed works in Western art. In a room of the Alcázar palace in Madrid, the five-year-old Infanta Margarita Teresa stands at the centre, attended by two maids of honour (the meninas), a chaperone, a bodyguard, the dwarfs Maribárbola and Nicolasito, and a sleepy mastiff. At the left, Velázquez himself stands at a huge canvas, brush in hand, wearing the red cross of the Order of Santiago, probably added after his knighthood in 1659. In a mirror on the back wall we see King Philip IV and Queen Mariana, apparently standing where we are. The picture raises endless questions about who is looking at whom and what is being painted. In 1957 Picasso painted 58 variations on it, now in the Museu Picasso in Barcelona.
creator: velazquez

title: The Milkmaid
note: A simple act of pouring milk made monumental by light and stillness.
image_file: Johannes Vermeer - Het melkmeisje - Google Art Project.png
description: In this small painting of about 1657–58, in the Rijksmuseum, a sturdy kitchen maid pours a thin stream of milk from a jug into an earthenware bowl, absorbed in her task. On the table are bread, a blue cloth and a jug, painted with sparkling dots of light. The bare wall behind her shows nail holes and a nail with its shadow. On the floor stand a foot-warmer and Delft tiles, one showing Cupid, perhaps a hint at the love associations of milkmaids in Dutch art. Vermeer used costly natural ultramarine in her apron. He turns an everyday action into an image of calm, almost sacred concentration.
creator: vermeer

title: View of Delft
note: A rare cityscape; Proust called it the most beautiful painting in the world.
image_file: Vermeer-view-of-delft.jpg
description: This cityscape of around 1660–61, in the Mauritshuis in The Hague, shows Delft seen from across the harbour to the south. Clouds cast shadows over the old city walls and gates in the foreground, while sunlight falls on the roofs and the tower of the New Church beyond. Vermeer used thick, granular paint, even mixing in sand, to suggest the texture of brick and stone, and pointillé dots on the boats. The novelist Marcel Proust considered it the most beautiful painting in the world. In his novel In Search of Lost Time, the writer Bergotte dies in front of it while admiring a 'little patch of yellow wall'.
creator: vermeer

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
note: A 'tronie' (character study) rather than a portrait of a known sitter.
image_file: 1665 Girl with a Pearl Earring.jpg
description: Painted around 1665, this is not a portrait of a known sitter but a tronie, a Dutch study of a face or character type. A young woman in an exotic blue and yellow turban turns over her shoulder to look at us, lips parted. A large pearl, painted with just a few strokes, glints at her ear. The background, now dark, was originally a deep green curtain, as a research project in 2018 revealed, along with fine eyelashes. The painting was sold at auction in 1881 for just a couple of guilders, and its buyer later bequeathed it to the Mauritshuis. Tracy Chevalier's 1999 novel and the 2003 film made it one of the most famous images in the world.
creator: vermeer

title: Pilgrimage to Cythera
note: His reception piece for the French Academy, which created the category of the fête galante for it.
image_file: L'Embarquement pour Cythère, by Antoine Watteau, from C2RMF retouched.jpg
description: This is the painting Watteau submitted to the Royal Academy in 1717. Its theme did not fit any existing category, so the Academy created a new one for him: the fête galante. Elegant couples, guided by flying cupids, are on the island of Cythera, sacred to Venus, whose garlanded statue stands at right. From right to left the couples seem to pass through the stages of courtship: being persuaded, rising and finally heading down to a golden boat. Scholars debate whether they are arriving or reluctantly leaving the island of love. The hazy landscape and gentle melancholy make it the key image of the Rococo. Watteau painted a second version, now in Berlin.
creator: watteau

title: The Swing
note: The quintessential Rococo image of flirtation and frivolity.
image_file: The Swing (P430).jpg
description: According to a contemporary memoir, a nobleman asked the painter Gabriel-François Doyen to paint his mistress on a swing pushed by a bishop, with himself placed where he could see her legs. The shocked Doyen passed the commission to Fragonard, who painted it in 1767. In a lush, overgrown garden, a young woman in a frothy pink dress swings high, kicking off her slipper towards a statue of Cupid, who holds a finger to his lips. Her lover hides in the bushes below, gazing up her skirts, while an elderly man, not a bishop in the final version, pushes the swing from the shadows. The painting is the quintessence of Rococo flirtation. A 2021 restoration at the Wallace Collection in London removed yellowed varnish and revealed its original bright colours.
creator: fragonard

title: Oath of the Horatii
note: Three brothers swear to fight for Rome: a manifesto of Neoclassical virtue.
image_file: Le Serment des Horaces - Jacques-Louis David - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 3692 ; MR 1432.jpg
description: Commissioned by the French royal government and painted in Rome in 1784, this canvas illustrates a legend from early Roman history. Rome and Alba Longa decided to settle a war by a fight between three brothers from each side: the Horatii and the Curiatii. In a stark hall with three Doric arches, the three Horatii brothers stretch out their arms to swear an oath on the swords their father holds up, pledging to fight to the death for Rome. At the right, the women of the family collapse in grief. One sister is engaged to one of the Curiatii, and another woman is a Curiatius married to a Horatius. The contrast between the rigid, straight lines of the men and the soft curves of the women dramatises the conflict between duty to the state and personal feeling. Shown at the 1785 Salon, it became the manifesto of Neoclassicism. It is in the Louvre.
creator: david

title: The Death of Marat
location: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels
note: The murdered revolutionary presented as a secular martyr.
image_file: Death of Marat by David.jpg
description: On 13 July 1793 the radical revolutionary journalist Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed to death in his bath, where he spent hours soaking to soothe a skin disease, by Charlotte Corday, a supporter of the rival Girondin faction. His friend David painted him within months as a martyr of the Revolution. Marat slumps in the bath, his arm hanging down like Christ's in a Deposition, with a quill still in his hand and Corday's deceitful letter in the other. The wooden crate beside him bears the dedication 'À Marat, David'. The upper half of the canvas is empty and dark. Stripped of almost all detail, it is a powerful piece of political propaganda and a deeply moving image. It is now in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium in Brussels.
creator: david

title: Psyche Revived by Cupid's Kiss
note: Interlocking figures form an elegant X of embrace.
image_file: 0 Psyché ranimée par le baiser de l'Amour - Canova - Louvre 1.JPG
description: Commissioned in 1787 by the British collector Colonel John Campbell and completed in 1793, this marble group in the Louvre is based on the tale of Cupid and Psyche from Apuleius's Golden Ass. Psyche has opened a forbidden flask and fallen into a deathlike sleep. Cupid descends and revives her with a kiss. The two bodies form an elegant X: her arms rise to encircle his head, and his outspread wings frame the composition. The moment just before the kiss creates a delicate tension. The flawless polish of the marble makes skin appear soft and luminous. A second version is in the Hermitage in St Petersburg.
creator: canova

title: La Grande Odalisque
note: Critics noticed her impossibly long back; Ingres valued line and elegance over anatomy.
image_file: La grande odalisque - Jean-Auguste Dominique Ingres - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 1158.jpg
description: Ingres painted this nude in Rome in 1814 for Caroline Murat, Napoleon's sister and Queen of Naples, but she never received it because the Murats fell from power. A concubine of the harem (an odalisque) reclines on a couch with her back to us and turns her head to look over her shoulder. She holds a peacock-feather fan, and a hookah stands nearby. When the painting was shown at the Salon of 1819, critics complained that her back was too long: she seems to have two or three extra vertebrae, and her arm and pelvis are distorted. Ingres sacrificed anatomy for a long, sinuous line and cool, smooth sensuality. The Louvre bought it in 1899.
creator: ingres

title: The Third of May 1808
note: French soldiers execute Spanish civilians; a founding image of modern anti-war art.
image_file: El Tres de Mayo, by Francisco de Goya, from Prado thin black margin.jpg
description: On 2 May 1808 the people of Madrid rose up against French occupation troops. The next night the French executed hundreds of civilians in reprisal. In 1814, after the French were expelled, Goya painted this scene and its companion, The Second of May. Under a dark sky, a faceless line of soldiers aims rifles at a group of prisoners lit by a large lantern. At the centre, a man in a white shirt flings his arms wide in a Christ-like pose, and marks resembling the stigmata appear on his palm. Others cover their eyes, pray or lie dead in blood. It is one of the first great paintings to show the horror of war without glory, and it influenced Manet's Execution of Maximilian and Picasso's Guernica. It is in the Prado.
creator: goya

title: Saturn Devouring His Son
note: One of the 'Black Paintings' Goya painted on the walls of his own house.
image_file: Francisco de Goya, Saturno devorando a su hijo (1819-1823).jpg
description: Between 1819 and 1823, Goya, now old, deaf and disillusioned, painted 14 dark murals directly on the plaster walls of his house outside Madrid, known as the Quinta del Sordo ('House of the Deaf Man'). This image, painted in the dining room, shows the Roman god Saturn (Kronos), who devoured his children for fear that one of them would overthrow him. Out of the black, a wild-eyed giant tears into the headless, bloody body of a child. The scene has been read as a symbol of time, of the destruction of Spain by its rulers, or of Goya's own despair. The titles were given by others after his death. In the 1870s the murals were transferred to canvas, and they were donated to the Prado in 1881.
creator: goya

title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
note: A lone figure seen from behind facing the sublime: the icon of Romanticism.
image_file: Caspar David Friedrich - Wanderer above the Sea of Fog.jpeg
description: Painted around 1818 and now in the Hamburger Kunsthalle, this small painting has become the definitive image of Romanticism. A man in a dark green frock coat stands with his back to us on a rocky summit, leaning on a stick. He looks out over a sea of fog from which rocky peaks and distant mountains emerge. We see what he sees, and we are left to imagine his thoughts and feelings in the face of nature's vastness. The landscape is a composite of studies made in the Elbe Sandstone Mountains. The figure has been interpreted as a self-portrait, an image of the individual before God, or a memorial to a fallen officer.
creator: friedrich

title: The Raft of the Medusa
note: Survivors of a real 1816 shipwreck, painted at the scale of history painting.
image_file: JEAN LOUIS THÉODORE GÉRICAULT - La Balsa de la Medusa (Museo del Louvre, 1818-19).jpg
description: In July 1816 the French frigate Méduse ran aground off the coast of Mauritania through the incompetence of its captain, a returned aristocrat appointed by the restored monarchy. About 150 people were left on a makeshift raft. During 13 days adrift, they suffered starvation, madness, murder and cannibalism, and only 15 survived. Géricault interviewed survivors, built a model of the raft, and studied corpses and severed limbs in hospitals. His huge canvas, about 5 by 7 metres, shows the moment the survivors sight a distant ship on the horizon. The figures rise in a pyramid from the dead and despairing to a Black man waving a cloth. Shown at the 1819 Salon, it was both a political scandal and a manifesto of Romanticism. It is in the Louvre.
creator: gericault

title: The Hay Wain
note: A cart fords a river in Suffolk; it won a gold medal at the 1824 Paris Salon.
image_file: John Constable - The Hay Wain (1821).jpg
description: Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1821 as Landscape: Noon, this large canvas shows a horse-drawn hay cart (wain) crossing a ford in the River Stour at Flatford Mill in Suffolk. Constable knew the spot intimately since childhood. At the left stands the cottage of the farmer Willy Lott, and on the right, beyond the trees, haymakers work in sunlit meadows under a vast sky of clouds. Constable worked up the composition from a full-size oil sketch, and his flickering white highlights convey sparkling light on water and leaves. The painting failed to sell in England, but at the Paris Salon of 1824 it won a gold medal from Charles X and inspired Delacroix and other French painters. It is in the National Gallery, London.
creator: constable

title: Liberty Leading the People
note: Commemorates the July Revolution of 1830; Liberty strides over the barricade with the tricolour.
image_file: La Liberté guidant le peuple - Eugène Delacroix - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 129 - après restauration 2024.jpg
description: This painting commemorates the July Revolution of 27–29 July 1830, the 'Three Glorious Days' in which Parisians overthrew King Charles X. Over a barricade of rubble and corpses, a bare-breasted woman, the personification of Liberty in a red Phrygian cap, holds aloft the tricolour flag and a musket and urges the people forward. Around her are a man in a top hat, possibly Delacroix himself, a worker with a sabre and a boy brandishing two pistols. The French state bought it in 1831, but it was soon hidden away as too inflammatory. Today it is a national symbol, used on the 100-franc banknote and in countless political images. It is in the Louvre, which restored it in 2023–24, revealing its original colours.
creator: delacroix

title: The Fighting Temeraire
note: A veteran warship towed to be broken up beneath a blazing sunset.
image_file: The Fighting Temeraire, JMW Turner, National Gallery.jpg
description: HMS Temeraire was a 98-gun warship that fought heroically at the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805. In 1838 the decommissioned ship was towed by a steam tug up the Thames to Rotherhithe to be broken up. Turner exhibited his painting of the scene in 1839. The ghostly old ship glides upriver behind a squat, black, smoke-belching tug, while the sun sets in a blaze of red and gold on the right. It is a poetic elegy for the age of sail and of Britain's naval glory, giving way to the age of steam. Turner called it his 'darling' and refused to sell it. It came to the National Gallery with the Turner Bequest and was voted Britain's greatest painting in a 2005 BBC poll.
creator: turner

title: Rain, Steam and Speed – The Great Western Railway
note: A train rushes through rain and mist: modern speed as Romantic subject.
image_file: Rain Steam and Speed the Great Western Railway.jpg
description: Exhibited in 1844, this painting shows a steam train on Isambard Kingdom Brunel's Maidenhead Railway Bridge over the Thames, rushing towards the viewer through rain and mist. The engine's black funnel and the bridge are almost the only solid forms in a swirling haze of golden and grey light. A hare runs on the tracks in front of the train, perhaps a symbol of natural speed outpaced by the machine. A ploughman works in a field and boaters drift on the river below. Turner captured modern technology and the sensation of speed in an almost abstract way. It is in the National Gallery, London.
creator: turner

title: A Burial at Ornans
note: A village funeral painted at a scale reserved for heroes; a Realist manifesto.
image_file: Gustave Courbet - A Burial at Ornans - Google Art Project 2.jpg
description: This enormous canvas, more than 6 metres wide, was painted in 1849–50 and shown at the Salon of 1850–51. It depicts the funeral of an ordinary person in Courbet's home town in the Jura. About 45 life-size townspeople, including the mayor, the priest, gravediggers, mourning women and Courbet's own father and sisters, gather around an open grave beneath grey cliffs. There is no heavenly vision and no heroic story, only the reality of provincial life and death. Critics were outraged that such a 'vulgar' subject was given the scale of history painting. The work became a manifesto of Realism. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: courbet

title: The Painter's Studio
note: Subtitled 'a real allegory' of seven years of his artistic life.
image_file: Courbet LAtelier du peintre.jpg
description: Courbet's full title for this vast work of 1855 is The Painter's Studio: A Real Allegory Summing Up a Seven-Year Phase of My Artistic and Moral Life. At the centre he sits painting a landscape, watched by a nude model and a small boy. At the left are figures representing society and its victims and exploiters: a hunter, a rabbi, a laborer, a prostitute, a priest and others. At the right are his friends and supporters, including the poet Baudelaire reading, the socialist philosopher Proudhon, the critic Champfleury and his patron Alfred Bruyas. The jury of the 1855 World's Fair rejected it, and Courbet showed it in his own Pavilion of Realism. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: courbet

title: The Gleaners
note: Three peasant women gather leftover grain, given monumental dignity.
image_file: Jean-François Millet - Gleaners - Google Art Project 2.jpg
description: Shown at the Salon of 1857, this painting shows three peasant women bending over the stubble of a harvested field to pick up the stray stalks of wheat left behind. Gleaning was a right granted to the poorest members of the rural community. In the bright background, a huge harvest is being loaded under the eye of an overseer on horseback. The women's heavy, monumental bodies and rhythmic poses give their back-breaking labour a timeless, almost religious dignity. Conservative critics saw it as a dangerous socialist reminder of rural poverty after the 1848 revolution. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: millet

title: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe
note: Shown at the Salon des Refusés; a nude woman picnics with clothed men.
image_file: Edouard Manet - Luncheon on the Grass - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Rejected by the official Salon jury, this large painting was shown in 1863 at the Salon des Refusés, an exhibition of rejected works ordered by Napoleon III, where it caused a scandal. In a woodland clearing, a nude woman picnics with two fully dressed young men in modern clothes, and she gazes boldly at the viewer, while a second woman bathes in the background. The model was Victorine Meurent, and the men were Manet's brother and his future brother-in-law. The composition borrows from a Renaissance engraving after Raphael and from Titian's Pastoral Concert, but by putting the nude in a contemporary setting and painting her with flat light, Manet made the scene shockingly modern. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: manet

title: Olympia
note: A modern courtesan in Titian's Venus pose, staring out at the viewer; a scandal at the 1865 Salon.
image_file: Edouard Manet - Olympia - Google Art ProjectFXD.jpg
description: Painted in 1863 and shown at the 1865 Salon, Olympia reworks Titian's Venus of Urbino as a modern Parisian prostitute. The model, again Victorine Meurent, reclines naked on a bed wearing only a black ribbon at her throat, a bracelet, an orchid in her hair and a single slipper. She stares directly and unashamedly at the viewer as if at a client. A Black maid brings a bouquet, probably from an admirer, and a black cat, replacing Titian's faithful dog, arches its back at the foot of the bed. The flat, harshly lit body and frank subject outraged critics and the public, and guards had to protect the painting from attack. In 1890 Claude Monet raised a public subscription to buy it for the French state. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: manet

title: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
note: His last major work; the mirror's reflection deliberately does not add up.
image_file: "Un Bar aux Folies-Bergère" by Édouard Manet (1882).jpg
description: Manet's last major painting, shown at the Salon of 1882, is set in the famous Parisian music hall. A barmaid stands behind a marble counter loaded with champagne, bottles of English Bass beer, a bowl of oranges and flowers. Behind her, a mirror reflects the glittering crowded hall, a chandelier and the green-booted legs of a trapeze artist at the top left. But the reflection doesn't match. The barmaid's reflection appears too far to the right, talking to a man in a top hat who should be standing where we are. Her detached expression contrasts with the bustle, and the painting has been read as a meditation on modern alienation and commerce. The collector Samuel Courtauld bought it in 1926, and it is in the Courtauld Gallery, London.
creator: manet

title: Impression, Sunrise
note: The harbour of Le Havre; a critic's mocking review gave Impressionism its name.
image_file: Monet - Impression, Sunrise.jpg
description: Monet painted this view of the port of Le Havre, his home town, in the early morning, probably in 1872. Through the mist and smoke of the industrial harbour, an orange sun rises over the water, and its reflection forms a broken line of orange strokes. Small rowing boats appear as dark silhouettes. The painting was shown at the first independent group exhibition in Paris in 1874. The critic Louis Leroy seized on its title to mock the whole group as 'Impressionists', and the name stuck. It was stolen from the Musée Marmottan in 1985 and recovered in 1990.
creator: monet

title: Water Lilies (Nymphéas) murals
note: Immersive panoramas of his Giverny pond, installed after his death.
image_file: Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond.jpg
description: In his last decades Monet painted his water garden at Giverny obsessively, producing around 250 paintings of water lilies. After the Armistice of November 1918 he offered the French state a monumental ensemble of water lily paintings as a monument to peace. With the help of his friend Georges Clemenceau, it was installed in two oval rooms in the Musée de l'Orangerie in Paris, which opened in 1927, a few months after his death. The eight huge panels, each about two metres high and together about 100 metres long, surround the visitor with the surface of the pond: water, lilies, reflected clouds, willows, at different times of day. They are often seen as the first immersive installation and a forerunner of abstract painting.
creator: monet
image_caption: Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond, c. 1920, Museum of Modern Art, New York: a related triptych, not the Orangerie cycle

title: The Cradle
note: Her sister watches over a sleeping baby; shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.
image_file: Berthe Morisot 008.jpg
description: Morisot painted this picture in 1872. It shows her elder sister Edma, who had given up painting after her marriage, watching over her sleeping baby daughter Blanche. A gauzy white veil drawn across the cradle frames the child, and Edma's arm and gaze create a diagonal connecting mother and child. Its tender subject and delicate handling of whites and transparent fabric made it one of the most admired works at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874. The Louvre acquired it in 1930, and it is now in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: morisot

title: The Dance Class
note: Ballerinas waiting and stretching around their teacher, off-duty moments rather than performance.
image_file: Edgar Degas - The Ballet Class - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Degas painted this picture in 1873–76. It shows a rehearsal room at the Paris Opera, where the elderly ballet master Jules Perrot, leaning on his stick, conducts a lesson. Around him, dancers in white tutus with coloured sashes wait their turn, stretch, chat, adjust their costumes and scratch their backs. One sits on the piano at left, and a watering can on the floor was used to settle dust. The figures are scattered informally around the room, as if seen by an observer passing through. Degas showed it at the Impressionist exhibition of 1876. A similar version is in the Metropolitan Museum. This one is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: degas

title: Little Dancer Aged Fourteen
type: Wax sculpture with fabric and hair
location: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C. (original wax)
note: Real tutu and hair ribbon shocked viewers; bronze casts were made after his death.
image_file: The Little Fourteen-Year-Old Dancer MET DP-14939-005.jpg
description: This is the only sculpture Degas ever exhibited. He showed it at the Impressionist exhibition of 1881. It shows Marie van Goethem, a young Belgian student of the Paris Opera ballet school, standing in the fourth position with her hands clasped behind her back and her chin raised. Degas modelled it in wax and dressed it in a real fabric bodice, a tulle tutu, satin slippers and a wig of real hair tied with a silk ribbon. Critics were shocked by its realism and called the girl ugly and coarse. After Degas's death, around 28 bronze casts were made from the wax, which is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
creator: degas
image_caption: Posthumous bronze cast, Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
note: Sunday dancing in Montmartre under dappled light.
image_file: Renoir, Pierre-Auguste - Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette, 1876.jpg
description: In 1876 Renoir rented a studio in Montmartre so that he could paint on the spot at the Moulin de la Galette, an open-air dance hall and café beside one of the old windmills on the hill, where working-class Parisians came to dance on Sunday afternoons. His friends posed among the crowd. Sunlight filtered through the trees falls in patches on the dancers, hats and faces, dissolving forms into a shimmer of colour and movement. Gustave Caillebotte bought the painting, and it entered the French national collection with his bequest. It is now in the Musée d'Orsay. A smaller version sold at auction in 1990 for one of the highest prices ever paid for a painting at the time.
creator: renoir

title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
note: Renoir's friends relax on a riverside balcony at Chatou.
image_file: Pierre-Auguste Renoir - Luncheon of the Boating Party - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted in 1880–81, this painting shows Renoir's friends relaxing after lunch on the balcony of the Maison Fournaise, a restaurant on an island in the Seine at Chatou, popular with boaters. At the left, the seamstress Aline Charigot, his future wife, plays with a small dog. At the right, the painter Gustave Caillebotte sits astride a chair in a white boating shirt. The tablecloth, glasses and bottles, the striped awning and the river beyond create a festive atmosphere. The American collector Duncan Phillips bought it in 1923, and it is the centrepiece of the Phillips Collection in Washington, D.C.
creator: renoir

title: The Thinker
note: Originally Dante contemplating his poem, atop The Gates of Hell.
image_file: Le Penseur by Rodin (Kunsthalle Bielefeld) 2014-04-10.JPG
description: Rodin's Thinker was conceived around 1880 as a figure of the poet Dante, seated above the doorway of his monumental Gates of Hell and contemplating the circles of the Inferno below. A powerful nude man sits on a rock, his chin resting on the back of his hand and his whole body tense with the effort of thought. Rodin later exhibited it as an independent sculpture, and in 1902–04 he enlarged it to monumental size. In 1906 a cast was placed in front of the Panthéon in Paris. More than 20 large bronze casts are now in cities around the world, and one was placed on Rodin's own grave at Meudon. It has become a universal symbol of philosophy and intellectual effort.
creator: rodin

title: The Kiss
note: The lovers Paolo and Francesca from Dante's Inferno.
image_file: Rodin - Le Baiser 06.jpg
description: This sculpture of lovers in an embrace represents Paolo and Francesca from Dante's Inferno. Francesca, married to Paolo's brother, fell in love with him while they were reading together about Lancelot and Guinevere, and they were killed by her husband. Rodin originally designed the group for the Gates of Hell but removed it, perhaps because its happy sensuality did not fit the theme of suffering. The French state commissioned this large marble version, now in the Musée Rodin, in 1888. The book the lovers were reading is still visible in Paolo's hand. Other marble versions are in Tate and in Copenhagen.
creator: rodin

title: A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte
note: Pointillism's manifesto, built from countless dots of colour.
image_file: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Georges Seurat, 1884.jpg
description: Seurat worked on this huge canvas, about 2 by 3 metres, from 1884 to 1886, making some 60 drawings and oil studies on the spot. It shows Parisians of different classes relaxing on La Grande Jatte, an island in the Seine on the outskirts of Paris: strolling couples, a woman with a monkey on a leash, a girl skipping, soldiers, boaters and a man playing a horn. Seurat painted it with tiny dots and dashes of contrasting colour, according to scientific colour theories, and later added a painted border of dots. The stiff, statue-like figures give the scene a strange, frozen solemnity. It caused a sensation at the last Impressionist exhibition of 1886, and it is in the Art Institute of Chicago. It inspired Stephen Sondheim's musical Sunday in the Park with George (1984).
creator: seurat

title: The Basket of Apples
note: A tilting table and shifting viewpoints that anticipate Cubism.
image_file: Paul Cézanne - The Basket of Apples - 1926.252 - Art Institute of Chicago.jpg
description: In this still life of around 1893, in the Art Institute of Chicago, a basket tipped forward spills apples across a table covered with a rumpled white cloth. A wine bottle leans at an angle, and a plate of biscuits sits at the back. Nothing is quite stable: the front edge of the table does not line up from left to right, the bottle tilts, and the plate seems seen from above while the basket is seen from the side. Cézanne combined several viewpoints and adjusted forms to create a dynamic balance of colour and structure, an approach that led directly to Cubism.
creator: cezanne

title: Mont Sainte-Victoire (series)
note: Dozens of views of the mountain near Aix, increasingly built from planes of colour.
image_file: Paul Cézanne - Montagne Saint-victoire - Google Art Project.jpg
description: The limestone mountain of Sainte-Victoire rises east of Aix-en-Provence, Cézanne's home town. From the early 1880s until his death in 1906 he painted it in dozens of oils and watercolours, from various viewpoints, including his last studio at Les Lauves. In the early versions the mountain appears behind valleys, fields, viaducts and pine trees, rendered with careful patches of colour. In the late versions it dissolves into a mosaic of almost abstract blocks of green, ochre and blue. For Cézanne the mountain was a lifelong motif for exploring how to build space, structure and light through colour. Versions are in museums around the world, from Philadelphia to the Courtauld and Moscow.
creator: cezanne

title: Vision after the Sermon
note: Breton women see Jacob wrestling the angel on a flat red field.
image_file: La vision après le sermon (Paul Gauguin).jpg
description: Painted in Pont-Aven in 1888, this is one of the founding works of Symbolism and of Gauguin's mature style. A group of Breton women in white headdresses, having just heard a sermon, have a vision of the biblical story of Jacob wrestling with the angel. The boundary between the real women in the foreground and their vision is a diagonal tree trunk. The ground is a flat, unnatural field of vermilion. Its bold outlines, flat colour and cropped composition show the influence of Japanese prints and of Émile Bernard. Gauguin offered it to a local church, which refused it. It is in the Scottish National Gallery, Edinburgh.
creator: gauguin

title: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
note: A large Tahitian frieze he considered his testament, read from right to left.
image_file: Gauguin - Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going? (1897-98).jpg
description: Gauguin painted this huge frieze, nearly four metres wide, in Tahiti in 1897–98, during a period of illness, poverty and grief after the death of his daughter Aline. He considered it his testament. It is meant to be read from right to left: a sleeping baby and young women at the right represent the beginning of life; a central figure picking fruit represents adult life and experience; and an old woman crouched in despair at the far left represents the approach of death. A mysterious blue idol presides in the background. In his letters, Gauguin said he attempted suicide after finishing it. It is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
creator: gauguin

title: Sunflowers
location: National Gallery, London (one of several versions)
note: Painted in Arles to decorate the room for Gauguin's visit.
image_file: Vincent Willem van Gogh 127.jpg
description: In August 1888 in Arles, Van Gogh painted a series of still lifes of sunflowers in a vase to decorate the room where Paul Gauguin would stay in his 'Yellow House'. He later made repetitions of them. This version, the fourth, in the National Gallery, London, shows 15 sunflowers at all stages of life, from fresh blooms to withered seed heads, painted in thick, textured strokes of yellow on yellow, with the vase signed 'Vincent'. Yellow, for Van Gogh, was the colour of happiness and the southern sun. Other versions are in Amsterdam, Munich, Philadelphia and Tokyo. The Tokyo version was bought at auction in 1987 for what was then a record price.
creator: van-gogh

title: The Bedroom
location: Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam (first of three versions)
note: His room in the Yellow House, meant to express 'absolute rest'.
image_file: Vincent van Gogh - De slaapkamer - Google Art Project.jpg
description: In October 1888 Van Gogh painted his own bedroom in the Yellow House in Arles. In a letter to Theo he explained that the colour was meant to suggest rest or sleep and to give a sense of calm. The room is shown in flat, bold colours: blue walls, a yellow bed and chairs, a red blanket, and a green window, with a skewed, steep perspective. The furniture, including two chairs and two pillows, has been read as a hope for companionship. When this first version was damaged by flooding, he painted two more at the asylum in Saint-Rémy, now in the Art Institute of Chicago and the Musée d'Orsay. This one is in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
creator: van-gogh

title: The Starry Night
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: Painted from memory at the asylum in Saint-Rémy; a swirling night sky above a village.
image_file: Van Gogh - Starry Night - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Van Gogh painted this canvas in June 1889 while a voluntary patient at the asylum of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence. It is based on the view from his east-facing window before sunrise, but he painted it during the day in his studio, from memory and imagination. A tall, flame-like cypress tree rises in the foreground. Below, a quiet village sleeps, with a church spire more Dutch than Provençal. Above, the night sky churns with swirling spirals, a radiant crescent moon and glowing stars, including the morning star Venus. Van Gogh himself was not satisfied with it. It is now one of the most famous paintings in the world, in the Museum of Modern Art, New York.
creator: van-gogh

title: The Scream
note: One of several versions; a universal image of modern anxiety.
image_file: Edvard Munch, 1893, The Scream, oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard, 91 x 73 cm, National Gallery of Norway.jpg
description: Munch described an experience while walking at sunset along a road above the Oslo fjord: the sky turned blood-red, and he felt what he called an infinite scream passing through nature. In The Scream, a skull-like figure on a bridge clasps its face and seems to scream, or to hear a scream, while two figures walk away behind it. The blood-red sky and the blue fjord swirl in rhythmic lines. Munch made several versions: this painting in tempera and crayon on cardboard of 1893, in the National Museum in Oslo; a crayon drawing and a later painting in the Munch Museum; a pastel of 1895, sold in 2012 for nearly $120 million; and a lithograph. Research in 2021 confirmed that a pencil note on this version saying it could only have been painted by a madman was written by Munch himself. Two versions have been stolen and recovered, in 1994 and 2004. It has become a universal image of modern anxiety.
creator: munch

title: Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I
type: Oil, silver and gold on canvas
note: Looted by the Nazis and returned to the family heirs in 2006.
image_file: Gustav Klimt, 1907, Adele Bloch-Bauer I, Neue Galerie New York.jpg
description: Klimt painted Adele Bloch-Bauer, the wife of the wealthy Jewish sugar industrialist Ferdinand Bloch-Bauer and a leading figure of Viennese society, in 1907, at the height of his golden phase. Her face, shoulders and hands are painted realistically, but her body and the background are dissolved into a dazzling surface of gold and silver leaf, decorated with Egyptian eye motifs, spirals and symbols. After the Nazis annexed Austria in 1938, the painting was seized and later displayed in the Austrian Gallery Belvedere. Adele's niece, Maria Altmann, fought for its return in a case that reached the US Supreme Court in 2004, and an arbitration panel ruled in her favour in 2006. Ronald Lauder then bought it for the Neue Galerie in New York. The story was told in the 2015 film Woman in Gold.
creator: klimt

title: The Kiss
type: Oil and gold leaf on canvas
note: The high point of his golden phase.
image_file: The Kiss - Gustav Klimt - Google Cultural Institute.jpg
description: Painted in 1907–08, The Kiss shows a couple locked in an embrace at the edge of a flowery meadow that ends abruptly at a cliff. The man, his face hidden, bends to kiss the woman's cheek. She kneels with her eyes closed, her hand around his neck. They are enveloped in a single golden robe: his decorated with black and white rectangles, hers with colourful circles and flowers, symbolising male and female. The Austrian state bought the painting in 1908 at the Kunstschau exhibition, even before it was finished. It is the most famous work of Viennese Art Nouveau and the highlight of the Belvedere in Vienna.
creator: klimt

title: Woman with a Hat
location: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
note: Shown at the 1905 Salon d'Automne that gave the Fauves ('wild beasts') their name.
image_file: Matisse-Woman-with-a-Hat.jpg
description: Matisse painted this portrait of his wife, Amélie, in 1905. She wears an elaborate hat and holds a fan. Her face is modelled not with natural flesh tones but with streaks of green, yellow, mauve and orange, and the background is an explosion of loose patches of colour. At the 1905 Salon d'Automne, it hung in a room with works by Derain, Vlaminck and others, and the critic Louis Vauxcelles called them 'fauves' (wild beasts). The painting caused a scandal, but it was bought by Leo and Gertrude Stein, which helped launch Matisse's career. It is now in the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art.
creator: matisse

title: Dance
note: Five red figures dance in a ring on blue and green; commissioned by Sergei Shchukin.
image_file: Matissedance.jpg
description: In 1909 the Moscow textile magnate Sergei Shchukin commissioned two large decorative panels, Dance and Music, for the staircase of his mansion. In Dance, completed in 1910, five red nude figures dance hand in hand in a circle on a green hill against a deep blue sky. The image is reduced to three colours and simplified, rhythmic outlines that seem to pulse with energy, recalling ancient vase painting and folk dances. When it was shown at the Paris Salon d'Automne in 1910, it was widely mocked. After the Russian Revolution Shchukin's collection was nationalised, and Dance is now in the Hermitage in St Petersburg. A preparatory version, Dance (I), is in the Museum of Modern Art, New York.
creator: matisse

title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: Fractured, mask-like figures; the breakthrough toward Cubism.
description: Picasso worked on this large canvas in his Paris studio over several months in 1907, making hundreds of preparatory drawings. It shows five nude women, prostitutes in a brothel on the Carrer d'Avinyó in Barcelona, confronting the viewer, with a still life of fruit at the bottom. Their bodies are made of sharp, angular planes. Some faces recall ancient Iberian sculpture, and the two at the right resemble African and Oceanic masks, which Picasso saw at the Trocadéro ethnographic museum in Paris. Even Picasso's friends were shocked, and he did not exhibit it publicly until 1916. It has been called a turning point in modern art and a starting point for Cubism. The Museum of Modern Art in New York acquired it in 1939.
creator: picasso

title: Guernica
note: A response to the bombing of the Basque town during the Spanish Civil War.
description: In January 1937 the government of the Spanish Republic, then fighting General Franco's Nationalists in the Spanish Civil War, commissioned Picasso to paint a mural for its pavilion at the Paris World's Fair. On 26 April 1937 German and Italian aircraft bombed the Basque town of Guernica in support of Franco. Picasso painted the huge canvas, nearly 8 metres wide, in about five weeks, and his partner Dora Maar photographed its progress. In a monochrome palette of black, white and grey that evokes newspaper photographs, a bull, a screaming horse, a mother holding her dead child, a dismembered soldier and figures in flames are crowded under a harsh electric light. At Picasso's request it was kept at the Museum of Modern Art in New York until democracy was restored in Spain, and it arrived in Madrid in 1981. Since 1992 it has been in the Museo Reina Sofía.
creator: picasso

title: Violin and Candlestick
location: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
note: Analytic Cubism: the objects dissolve into overlapping grey-brown facets.
description: Painted in 1910 at the height of Analytic Cubism, this painting in the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art breaks a still life of a violin and a candlestick into overlapping fragments of planes and facets in muted browns and greys, so that object and space merge. Fragments of the violin's scroll, strings and f-holes can be made out at the lower left, and the candlestick's base and flame at the centre. The painting shows several viewpoints at once and invites the viewer to reconstruct the objects in the mind.
creator: braque

title: Composition VII
note: A major early abstract painting, prepared through more than 30 studies.
image_file: Composition VII - Wassily Kandinsky, GAC.jpg
description: Kandinsky regarded his ten Compositions, painted between 1910 and 1939, as his most important works, carefully prepared summations of his ideas. Composition VII, painted in Munich in 1913 after more than 30 preparatory drawings, watercolours and oil studies, is about 2 by 3 metres. It is a whirlwind of colour, lines and forms in which traces of biblical themes such as the Resurrection, the Last Judgement, the Flood and the Garden of Love have been almost entirely dissolved into abstraction. Kandinsky is said to have painted the final canvas in about four days. It is in the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
creator: kandinsky

title: Broadway Boogie Woogie
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: Manhattan's grid and jazz rhythm translated into pulsing coloured squares.
image_file: Piet Mondrian, 1942 - Broadway Boogie Woogie.jpg
description: Mondrian arrived in New York in 1940 and loved the city's energy and its boogie-woogie jazz. This painting of 1942–43, completed shortly before his death and bought by the Museum of Modern Art in 1943, abandons his usual black lines. Instead, a grid of yellow lines, broken by small squares of red, blue and grey, suggests the street grid of Manhattan, the flashing lights of Broadway, traffic and the syncopated rhythms of the music. A few larger blocks of colour float within the grid. His last, unfinished work, Victory Boogie Woogie, is in The Hague.
creator: mondrian

title: Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2
note: Caused a sensation at the 1913 Armory Show in New York.
description: Painted in 1912, this painting shows a figure walking down a spiral staircase broken into overlapping, mechanical-looking planes, like a sequence of photographs. It combines the fragmentation of Cubism with the analysis of motion in the chronophotographs of Étienne-Jules Marey and the Futurists, in browns and ochres. Fellow Cubists asked Duchamp to remove it from the 1912 Salon des Indépendants in Paris, perhaps because of its title and its suggestion of motion. At the 1913 Armory Show in New York it became the most notorious work, and a critic described it as 'an explosion in a shingle factory'. It is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
creator: duchamp

title: Fountain
location: Original lost; 1964 replicas in several museums, incl. Tate
note: Signed 'R. Mutt'; arguably the most influential artwork of the 20th century.
description: In April 1917 the Society of Independent Artists in New York announced an exhibition open to anyone who paid the fee. Duchamp, a member of its board, submitted a standard porcelain urinal, laid on its back and signed 'R. Mutt 1917'. The committee refused to show it, and it was hidden during the exhibition. The photographer Alfred Stieglitz photographed it, and the photograph appeared in a small magazine, The Blind Man, with an article arguing that the artist's choice is what makes something art. The original was lost. In 1964 Duchamp authorised a small edition of replicas, now in museums including Tate. In 2004 a poll of 500 art experts named it the most influential work of modern art. Some scholars have suggested that the Dada artist Elsa von Freytag-Loringhoven may have been involved in the idea, though this is debated.
creator: duchamp

title: The Treachery of Images ('Ceci n'est pas une pipe')
location: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
note: A picture of a pipe captioned 'This is not a pipe'.
description: Magritte painted this image in 1929. A carefully drawn pipe, like an image in an advertisement or a schoolbook, floats against a plain background, and below it is a neat handwritten caption in French: 'This is not a pipe.' The paradox is simple and profound: of course it is not a pipe, but a painted image of a pipe. The painting questions the relationship between objects, images and words, and the philosopher Michel Foucault wrote a famous essay on it. It is in the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
creator: magritte

title: The Son of Man
note: A bowler-hatted man whose face is hidden by a floating green apple.
description: Magritte painted this self-portrait in 1964 for his friend and patron, the lawyer Harry Torczyner. A man in an overcoat, red tie and bowler hat stands in front of a low wall with the sea and a cloudy sky behind him. His face is almost entirely hidden by a green apple floating in front of it, and only the edge of one eye peeps out. Magritte said that everything we see hides something else, and that we always want to see what is hidden by what we see. The title and the apple suggest Adam and the Fall. It is in a private collection and is one of the most reproduced images of Surrealism.
creator: magritte

title: The Persistence of Memory
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: Melting clocks in a dream landscape inspired by the Catalan coast.
description: This small painting of 1931, only about 24 by 33 cm, is one of the most famous images of Surrealism.
