In a dreamlike landscape based on the rocky coast of Cap de Creus near Dalí's home, pocket watches melt and droop over a tree branch, the edge of a table and a strange fleshy creature lying on the ground, which resembles Dalí's own profile with long eyelashes. Ants crawl over a closed orange watch. Dalí said the soft watches were inspired by Camembert cheese melting in the sun. The painting suggests the fluidity and unreliability of time and memory in dreams. It has been in the Museum of Modern Art in New York since 1934.
creator: dali

title: The Two Fridas
location: Museo de Arte Moderno, Mexico City
note: A double self-portrait joined by a shared artery, painted around her divorce from Diego Rivera.
museum_name: Museo de Arte Moderno, Mexico City
description: Kahlo painted this large double self-portrait, about 1.7 metres square, in 1939, around the time of her divorce from Diego Rivera. Two Fridas sit side by side holding hands under a stormy sky. At the right, the Frida in a Tehuana dress, which Rivera loved, holds a tiny portrait of him. At the left, the Frida in a white European Victorian dress tries to stop the bleeding from a severed artery with surgical forceps, and blood drips onto her skirt. Their exposed hearts are connected by a single vein. The painting expresses her divided identity, Mexican and European, loved and abandoned. It was shown at the International Surrealist Exhibition in Mexico City in 1940 and is in the Museo de Arte Moderno in Mexico City.
creator: kahlo

title: Nighthawks
note: Late-night customers in a glowing diner seen from a deserted street.
image_file: Nighthawks by Edward Hopper 1942.jpg
description: Hopper finished this painting in January 1942, shortly after the attack on Pearl Harbor. It shows a corner diner at night, seen through its large curved window from a deserted street. Inside, under harsh fluorescent light, a counterman in white serves three customers: a couple sitting side by side without speaking, and a man alone with his back to us. There is no visible door, which seals the figures inside the glass. Hopper said the diner was inspired by one on Greenwich Avenue in New York, simplified and enlarged, and admitted that unconsciously he was probably painting the loneliness of a big city. His wife Jo posed for the woman. The Art Institute of Chicago bought it a few months after it was painted, and it has become one of the most famous and parodied images of American art.
creator: hopper

title: Autumn Rhythm (Number 30)
location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: A large drip painting from the height of his career.
description: Pollock painted this huge canvas, more than 5 metres wide, at his studio in Springs, Long Island, in the autumn of 1950, at the height of his drip-painting period. He laid the unprimed canvas on the floor and poured and flung black, white, brown and teal enamel paint onto it with sticks and brushes, working from all sides. The result is a dense, rhythmic web of lines and splatters with no single focal point, which seems to extend beyond the edges of the canvas. It conveys the physical energy of its making. The Metropolitan Museum of Art acquired it in 1957, a year after Pollock's death.
creator: pollock

title: Rothko Chapel paintings
note: Dark, near-black canvases for a non-denominational chapel, which opened in 1971. Several panels were damaged by Hurricane Beryl in 2024 and have been undergoing conservation.
description: In 1964 the art collectors and philanthropists John and Dominique de Menil commissioned Rothko to create paintings for a non-denominational chapel in Houston. He worked on the 14 large canvases from 1964 to 1967 and was closely involved in the design of the octagonal building, although he died before it opened in 1971. The paintings, some single panels and some triptychs, are either black rectangles on deep maroon fields or monochrome purple tones, so dark that they reveal themselves only slowly to the eye. Together they create an atmosphere of meditation for people of all faiths. Barnett Newman's sculpture Broken Obelisk stands on the plaza outside. Several panels were damaged by Hurricane Beryl in 2024 and have been undergoing conservation.
creator: rothko

title: Campbell's Soup Cans
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: One canvas per flavour; supermarket goods as fine art.
description: In July 1962 Warhol's first solo exhibition of paintings, at the Ferus Gallery in Los Angeles, showed 32 canvases, one for each variety of soup then sold by Campbell's. The paintings were displayed side by side on a narrow shelf, like products in a supermarket. Each was painted by hand with the help of projection and a stamp for the fleur-de-lis pattern, but looks mass-produced, and only the label changes. The gallery owner Irving Blum bought the whole set for $1,000, paid in instalments. The paintings provoked debate about whether consumer goods could be the subject of fine art, and they made Warhol famous. The Museum of Modern Art acquired them in 1996.
creator: warhol

title: Marilyn Diptych
note: Made in the weeks after Marilyn Monroe's death; colour on one side, fading black-and-white on the other.
description: Marilyn Monroe died in August 1962. Within weeks, Warhol began silkscreening a publicity photograph of her from the 1953 film Niagara onto canvas. In the Marilyn Diptych, 50 images of her face are arranged in a grid across two panels. On the left, 25 images are printed in garish colours of yellow hair, pink skin and turquoise eye shadow. On the right, 25 are printed in black and white, increasingly smeared or faded, as if fading away. The work comments on celebrity, mass media, repetition and death. It was bought by the collectors Burton and Emily Tremaine, and Tate acquired it in 1980.
creator: warhol

title: Whaam!
note: A comic-book fighter-jet explosion blown up to monumental scale.
description: Painted in 1963, this large two-panel painting, about 4 metres wide, is based on a panel from a 1962 DC war comic, All-American Men of War. In the left panel, a fighter pilot fires a missile, with a speech balloon in the comic's style. In the right panel, an enemy plane explodes in a burst of red and yellow flame, with the giant onomatopoeic word 'WHAAM!'. Lichtenstein enlarged the comic image, simplified it and painted it with flat colours, black outlines and Ben-Day dots, giving a throwaway image the scale and presence of a history painting. Its acquisition by Tate in 1966 was controversial.
creator: lichtenstein

title: Discobolus (Discus Thrower)
location: Roman copies; the best-known marble (Lancellotti) is in the National Roman Museum, Palazzo Massimo, Rome
note: An athlete frozen at the top of his swing, balancing tension and calm.
image_file: Roman bronze copy of Myron’s Discobolos, 2nd century CE (Glyptothek Munich).jpg
description: Myron's bronze original of about 460–450 BC is lost, but its fame led the Romans to make many marble copies. The best known is the Lancellotti Discobolus, found in Rome in 1781, now in the Palazzo Massimo. The athlete is caught at the top of his backswing, the instant before he unwinds to throw. His body forms two interlocking arcs, like a drawn bow, yet his face is completely calm. The pose is not quite anatomically possible, which shows that Myron was designing a perfect image rather than recording a real movement. It has become a universal emblem of athletics and the Olympic ideal.
creator: myron

title: Doryphoros (Spear-Bearer)
location: National Archaeological Museum, Naples (copy from Pompeii)
note: The demonstration piece for his Canon of ideal proportions and contrapposto stance.
image_file: 02 10 2024 Photo Paolo Villa-Napoli-mann-Museo Archeologico-FO232526tris-Arte Greca copia romana-Policleto Doriforo Polykleitos Doryphoros from Pompeii-marmo marble carrara.jpg
description: The Doryphoros is generally identified as the statue Polykleitos made to demonstrate his Canon of ideal proportions. The bronze original is lost. The most complete Roman marble copy was found at Pompeii and is now in Naples. A powerfully built young man walks forward with his weight on his right leg. His relaxed left leg trails behind, his hips and shoulders tilt in opposite directions, and his left arm once held a spear over the shoulder. This balance of tense and relaxed limbs, called contrapposto or chiasmus, makes the figure look alive and poised even at rest. It became the model for countless later statues, from Roman emperors to Michelangelo's David.
creator: polykleitos

title: Parthenon Sculptures
location: Acropolis Museum, Athens, and British Museum, London
note: Made under Phidias's direction; the return of the British Museum portion is a long-running dispute.
image_file: Elgin-marbles-jan-2024.jpg
description: The Parthenon, built 447–432 BC as the temple of Athena, carried the most ambitious sculpture programme in Greek history, designed and supervised by Phidias. There were 92 carved metopes showing mythical battles; a continuous frieze about 160 metres long showing a procession in honour of Athena, probably the Panathenaic festival; and two pediments, showing Athena's birth and her contest with Poseidon for Athens. The figures combine idealised calm with a remarkable sense of breathing flesh under clinging drapery. Between 1801 and 1812 agents of Lord Elgin removed about half of the surviving sculpture to Britain, and it has been in the British Museum since 1816. Greece has long sought its return, and the Acropolis Museum, opened in 2009, displays its own portion with spaces left for the missing pieces.
creator: phidias

title: Aphrodite of Knidos
location: Roman copies, incl. Palazzo Altemps, Rome, and the Colonna Venus, Vatican Museums
note: The first monumental female nude in Greek sculpture, famous throughout antiquity.
image_file: Cnidus Aphrodite Altemps Inv8619.jpg
description: According to Pliny, Praxiteles made two statues of Aphrodite. The people of Kos chose the modestly draped one, and the city of Knidos bought the nude one, which made the city famous. The goddess is shown about to bathe, lowering her robe onto a water jar and lifting one hand before her body in a gesture later called the Venus Pudica (modest Venus). She stood in a round shrine that let visitors walk all the way around her, and ancient writers told stories of travellers overwhelmed by her beauty. The original is lost. Roman copies such as the Colonna Venus in the Vatican and the version in Rome's Palazzo Altemps preserve its composition, the first monumental fully nude goddess in Greek art.
creator: praxiteles

title: Laocoön and His Sons
note: Excavated in Rome in 1506 with Michelangelo present; a model of anguish and twisting form for Renaissance and Baroque artists.
image_file: Laocoön and his sons group.jpg
description: In Virgil's Aeneid, Laocoön was the Trojan priest who warned against the wooden horse. The gods sent two great sea serpents to crush him and his sons. The sculptors show the moment of agony: the father's body twists and strains, his face contorted, while the serpents coil around all three. The group was dug up in a Roman vineyard in January 1506. Michelangelo and the architect Giuliano da Sangallo identified it on the spot from Pliny's description, and Pope Julius II bought it for the Vatican's Belvedere courtyard. Laocoön's missing right arm was restored as stretched upward. The original bent arm was found by the archaeologist Ludwig Pollak in 1906 and reattached in the 1950s. The group inspired Renaissance and Baroque artists and Lessing's famous essay on the limits of painting and poetry, Laokoon (1766).
creator: laocoon-sculptors

title: Santa Trinita Maestà
note: A towering enthroned Virgin with angels, hung in the Uffizi beside Duccio's and Giotto's Madonnas for comparison.
image_file: Cimabue - Maestà di Santa Trinita - Google Art Project.jpg
description: This towering altarpiece, more than 3.8 metres high, was painted for the church of Santa Trinita in Florence. The Virgin sits enthroned with the Christ Child, surrounded by eight angels stacked up either side of the throne. Below, four Old Testament prophets look out from arches under the throne. The gold ground and stylised features follow Byzantine tradition. Cimabue gives the throne a sense of depth, the faces gentle individual expressions and the composition a new monumental structure. In the Uffizi it hangs in the same room as Duccio's Rucellai Madonna and Giotto's Ognissanti Madonna, so visitors can see the change from Byzantine to early Renaissance painting side by side.
creator: cimabue

title: Maestà
note: Carried in procession to Siena Cathedral; the back held dozens of scenes from Christ's life.
image_file: Duccio maesta1021.jpg
description: Siena was dedicated to the Virgin, and its cathedral commissioned Duccio in 1308 to paint a new high altarpiece. When it was finished in June 1311, the painting was carried from his workshop to the cathedral in a solemn procession with the whole city following, bells ringing and candles lit. The front shows the Virgin and Child enthroned among saints and angels, with Siena's four patron saints kneeling in front. The back held dozens of small scenes from the life and Passion of Christ, full of vivid storytelling. The altarpiece was sawn apart in 1771. Most of it is in Siena's cathedral museum, but some predella and back panels were sold and are now in London, New York, Washington and elsewhere.
creator: duccio

title: Gates of Paradise
location: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Florence (copies on the Baptistery)
note: Ten Old Testament panels in perspective; Michelangelo reportedly gave them their name.
image_file: Lorenzo Ghiberti-The Gates of Paradise - Original-Museo dell'Opera del Duomo (Florence).jpg
description: In 1425 Ghiberti was commissioned to make a third set of bronze doors for the Florence Baptistery, the east doors facing the cathedral. He worked on them until 1452. Abandoning the Gothic four-lobed frames of earlier doors, he made ten large square panels of gilded bronze telling Old Testament stories from Adam and Eve to Solomon and the Queen of Sheba. Each panel uses the new linear perspective to create deep architectural and landscape settings, with figures modelled from almost fully round in front to faint low relief at the back. Small heads in the frame include a self-portrait. Michelangelo reportedly said the doors were worthy to be the Gates of Paradise. After flood damage in 1966 and long restoration, the originals are now in the cathedral museum, and copies hang on the Baptistery.
creator: ghiberti

title: Dome of Florence Cathedral
note: Built without centring scaffolding using a double shell and herringbone brickwork; still the largest masonry dome in the world.
image_file: Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore – Il Duomo di Firenze.jpg
description: Florence Cathedral's octagonal crossing, about 45 metres across, had been planned at a size no one knew how to cover: it was too wide for the timber centring normally used to support a vault while it was built. In 1418 Brunelleschi won the competition with a radical proposal, and work ran from 1420 to 1436. His dome is made of two shells, an inner and an outer, linked by ribs. The bricks are laid in a herringbone pattern so the courses lock together and support themselves as the dome rises. He also invented new hoisting machines to lift around four million bricks and huge stones. The marble lantern on top was completed after his death to his design, and Verrocchio's workshop, where the young Leonardo was training, added the gilded ball in 1471. It remains the largest masonry dome ever built.
creator: brunelleschi

title: The Tribute Money
location: Brancacci Chapel, Santa Maria del Carmine, Florence
note: Solid figures, consistent light and atmospheric landscape in a single continuous narrative.
image_file: The Tribute Money by Masaccio.jpg
description: This fresco in the Brancacci Chapel tells the story from Matthew's Gospel in which a tax collector asks for the temple tax. In the centre, Christ tells Peter to find a coin in the mouth of a fish. At the left, Peter crouches by the lake to take it out, and at the right he pays the collector. This is 'continuous narrative', with one figure appearing three times in a single scene. The apostles stand around Christ like solid statues, their robes falling with real weight. Light comes consistently from the direction of the chapel's actual window, and the vanishing point of the building at right lies at Christ's head. The mountains fade into hazy distance, an early use of atmospheric perspective.
creator: masaccio

title: Holy Trinity
note: Among the earliest paintings to use mathematically correct linear perspective.
image_file: Masaccio, trinità.jpg
description: Painted on a wall of Santa Maria Novella around 1427, the Holy Trinity creates the illusion of a deep chapel opening into the church. It has a coffered barrel vault and classical columns that closely follow Brunelleschi's architecture, and it is among the earliest paintings constructed with mathematically correct perspective. God the Father stands behind the crucified Christ with the dove of the Holy Spirit between them, flanked by the Virgin and St John. The two donors kneel outside the painted chapel, in the viewer's space. Below lies a painted tomb with a skeleton and an inscription warning: 'I was once what you are, and what I am you also will be.'
creator: masaccio

title: Annunciation (San Marco)
note: Painted at the top of the dormitory stairs of the friars' convent.
image_file: Fra Angelico - Annunciation.jpg
description: Fra Angelico painted this fresco around 1440–45 at the top of the staircase leading to the friars' dormitory in the convent of San Marco, where every friar would see it daily. The angel Gabriel, with rainbow-coloured wings, kneels before the Virgin, who sits on a simple stool and crosses her arms in humble acceptance. The setting is a light, airy loggia with slender columns close to the convent's real architecture by Michelozzo, opening onto an enclosed garden that symbolises her purity. An inscription below asks those passing to say a Hail Mary. The picture's quiet colours and clear space were designed for contemplation.
creator: fra-angelico

title: The Baptism of Christ
note: Pale, still figures in a clear Tuscan landscape structured by geometry.
image_file: Piero della Francesca - Baptism of Christ - WGA17595.jpg
description: Probably painted in the 1450s for a chapel or priory in Piero's home town of Sansepolcro, this panel shows John the Baptist pouring water over Christ's head as the dove of the Holy Spirit hovers above. Christ stands perfectly still and upright, like a column, beside a walnut tree whose pale trunk echoes his body. Three angels watch at the left, and in the background a man pulls his shirt over his head before his own baptism. The figures' reflections appear in the still river, and the landscape is the hilly countryside around Sansepolcro. Its geometry, pale colour and calm make it one of the best-loved works of the Renaissance; it is in the National Gallery, London.
creator: piero

title: The Flagellation of Christ
note: A small panel famous for its perspective and its puzzling meaning.
image_file: Piero della Francesca - Flagelación de Cristo, 1468-1470 (Galleria Nazionale delle Marche, Urbino).png
description: This small panel of around 1455–60, in the Galleria Nazionale delle Marche in Urbino, is one of the most puzzling pictures of the Renaissance. In a classical hall at the left and rear, Christ is tied to a column and whipped while a seated ruler watches. In the right foreground, outside, three large figures stand talking, apparently paying no attention. Their identity has been debated for centuries: theories range from members of the Montefeltro court to an allusion to the fall of Constantinople in 1453. The architecture is built with such exact perspective that scholars have reconstructed its floor plan from the painting.
creator: piero

title: Camera degli Sposi
note: The ceiling's painted oculus is the first di sotto in sù (seen-from-below) illusion of the Renaissance.
image_file: Mantegna - Camera degli Sposi.jpg
description: Between 1465 and 1474 Mantegna frescoed a room in the Castello di San Giorgio, part of the Gonzaga palace in Mantua. It is now called the Camera degli Sposi ('Bridal Chamber'), though it was used as a reception and bedroom. The walls show Marquis Ludovico Gonzaga with his family, courtiers, servants and even a favourite dog, in one of the earliest group portraits of a court. The ceiling is the true marvel. Mantegna painted a circular opening, or oculus, to the sky, with women, a peacock and winged cherubs peering down over a balustrade. A plant pot balances precariously on the edge. It is the first di sotto in sù ('seen from below') ceiling illusion of the Renaissance and a model for Baroque ceilings.
creator: mantegna

title: Lamentation of Christ
note: The dead Christ in extreme, dramatic foreshortening.
image_file: The dead Christ and three mourners, by Andrea Mantegna.jpg
description: In this painting from around 1480, now in the Brera in Milan, the dead Christ lies on a marble slab seen from his feet. He is drastically foreshortened so that the wounds in his feet and hands are thrust towards the viewer. Mantegna actually shortened the legs and enlarged the head to make the image readable and heighten its impact. At the left, the weeping Virgin, St John and Mary Magdalene squeeze into the edge of the picture. The colours are muted, almost like stone. The painting was found in Mantegna's studio after his death, which suggests he kept it for his own devotion.
creator: mantegna

title: Saint Francis in the Desert
note: The saint stands in radiant light in a richly observed landscape.
image_file: Giovanni Bellini - Saint Francis in the Desert - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted around 1475–80 and now in the Frick Collection, New York, this panel shows St Francis of Assisi stepping out of his rocky cell. He stands barefoot with his arms spread and face lifted towards a radiant light at the upper left. Whether Bellini meant the moment he received the stigmata or simply an ecstatic hymn to Creation is debated. The landscape is observed with extraordinary care: a donkey, a heron, a rabbit peering from a hole, layered rocks, a walled town and distant blue hills. Everything is bathed in warm, golden light, and nature itself seems to share in the saint's spiritual experience.
creator: bellini

title: The Descent from the Cross
note: Life-size mourners in a shallow, shrine-like space; the swooning Virgin echoes Christ's pose.
image_file: El Descendimiento, by Rogier van der Weyden, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg
description: Painted around 1435 for the chapel of the Crossbowmen's Guild in Leuven, this panel compresses ten life-size figures into a shallow gold box, like a carved and painted altar shrine come to life. Small crossbows in the upper corners refer to the patrons. Christ's pale body is lowered from the cross, and the Virgin collapses in a faint that exactly echoes her son's pose, expressing her compassion: she suffers with him. Each mourner shows grief differently, and the tears are painted as glassy drops on their cheeks. The painting so impressed the Habsburgs that it was acquired by Mary of Hungary and later Philip II, which is how it reached the Prado.
creator: van-der-weyden

title: The Ambassadors
note: Two French envoys surrounded by scientific instruments; a distorted skull (anamorphosis) resolves from the side.
image_file: Hans Holbein the Younger - The Ambassadors - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted in London in 1533, this double portrait shows Jean de Dinteville, French ambassador to Henry VIII, and his friend Georges de Selve, Bishop of Lavaur. Between them stands a two-tiered table covered with scientific instruments, a globe, a lute with a broken string and a Lutheran hymn book. These symbols of learning and the arts may also hint at discord in religion and politics during the Reformation. Across the floor floats a strange diagonal shape. Seen from the right side, close to the wall, it resolves into a human skull, an anamorphic memento mori reminding the viewer of death. A tiny crucifix half-hidden by the curtain at top left offers the hope of salvation. The National Gallery bought it in 1890.
creator: holbein

title: The Tempest
note: One of the first paintings where landscape and weather set the mood; its subject is still unexplained.
image_file: Giorgione - Das Gewitter.jpg
description: This small painting of around 1506–08, in the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice, is one of the most mysterious in Western art. At the left a young man with a staff stands by broken columns. At the right a half-naked woman sits nursing a baby on the river bank and looks straight out at us. Between them, under a dark sky split by lightning, lies a town. X-rays show that Giorgione originally painted a bathing woman where the young man now stands, which suggests he invented as he went. In 1530 a Venetian collector described it simply as a 'little landscape with the storm, a gypsy and a soldier'. Interpretations range from Adam and Eve to classical myth, but its real subject may be the stormy atmosphere itself, which makes it a pioneer of landscape as mood.
creator: giorgione

title: Self-portrait in a Convex Mirror
note: Painted on a curved panel to mimic a barber's mirror, with an enlarged hand in the foreground.
image_file: Parmigianino Selfportrait.jpg
description: Painted around 1524, when Parmigianino was about 21, this self-portrait is on a wooden panel shaped like a section of a sphere, imitating the convex barber's mirror Vasari says he used as his model. His youthful face is undistorted at the centre, while his hand in the foreground swells enormously and the room behind curves around the edges. He took it to Rome as a showpiece and presented it to Pope Clement VII. It later belonged to the writer Pietro Aretino and is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna. It also inspired John Ashbery's prize-winning 1975 poem of the same name.
creator: parmigianino

title: Madonna with the Long Neck
note: A defining Mannerist image of elongation and elegance, left unfinished.
image_file: Parmigianino - Madonna and Child with Angels, known as the Madonna with the Long Neck.jpg
description: Commissioned in 1534 for a chapel in the church of Santa Maria dei Servi in Parma, this altarpiece was still unfinished when Parmigianino died in 1540. The Virgin, with a swan-like neck and tapering fingers, presides over an impossibly long, sleeping Christ Child, whose pose foreshadows the dead Christ of the Pietà. Crowded angels press in at the left, and in the strangely scaled background a tiny prophet unrolls a scroll beside a row of unfinished columns. The disproportion is deliberate: the elongated beauty refers to medieval poetic images of the Virgin's neck as an ivory tower, and it was meant to delight connoisseurs. It is now in the Uffizi.
creator: parmigianino

title: Venus, Cupid, Folly and Time
note: A cold, sensual and puzzling allegory made as a diplomatic gift for Francis I of France.
image_file: Angelo Bronzino - Venus, Cupid, Folly and Time - National Gallery, London.jpg
description: Bronzino painted this allegory around 1545 as a diplomatic gift from Cosimo I de' Medici to King Francis I of France. Venus, holding the golden apple, is embraced and kissed by her son Cupid in a disturbingly erotic way. Around them crowd strange personifications. A laughing boy is about to throw roses, perhaps Folly or Pleasure. Behind him a sweet-faced girl offers honey but has a serpent's tail, perhaps Fraud. A figure tears its hair in anguish, interpreted as Jealousy or as the effects of syphilis. Above, bald Father Time and a mask-like figure struggle over a blue curtain, threatening to reveal or hide the scene. The cold polished surfaces and puzzling meaning are typical of Mannerist court art. It is in the National Gallery, London.
creator: bronzino

title: The Last Supper (San Giorgio Maggiore)
note: The table recedes on a steep diagonal, lit by a smoky lamp and glowing angels.
image_file: Jacopo Tintoretto - The Last Supper - WGA22649.jpg
description: Tintoretto painted this canvas in 1592–94, at the end of his life, for the chancel of Palladio's church of San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice, where it still hangs. Rather than the calm frontal arrangement used by Leonardo, he set the table on a steep diagonal running into the dark depths of a tavern-like room. Christ, at the centre, gives bread to the apostles, his halo blazing. Servants busy themselves with food and dishes, and a cat pokes into a basket. Smoke from a hanging oil lamp turns into the ghostly forms of angels swirling overhead, merging the everyday and the supernatural in one dramatic image of the Eucharist.
creator: tintoretto

title: The Laughing Cavalier
note: A confident sitter with a famous moustache and lavishly embroidered sleeve; he is smiling, not laughing.
image_file: Cavalier soldier Hals-1624x.jpg
description: An inscription records that this sitter was 26 years old in 1624, but his identity is unknown. The title is a Victorian invention: he is not laughing, though his raised eyebrows, upturned moustache and confident pose with his hand on his hip give him a cocky, amused air. The real showpiece is his richly embroidered sleeve, painted with dazzling freedom. It is decorated with motifs of arrows, flaming cornucopias, lovers' knots and bees, symbols of the pleasures and pains of love that suggest it may have been painted for a betrothal. The 4th Marquess of Hertford bought it in a famous Paris auction in 1865, and it is now one of the best-loved works in the Wallace Collection in London.
creator: hals

title: Et in Arcadia ego
note: Shepherds discover a tomb inscribed 'Even in Arcadia, I [Death] am present'.
image_file: Nicolas Poussin - Et in Arcadia ego (deuxième version).jpg
description: In this painting of around 1637–38 in the Louvre, three shepherds in an idyllic Arcadian landscape have discovered a tomb. One kneels to trace with his finger the inscription 'Et in Arcadia ego' ('Even in Arcadia, I am here'), meaning that Death is present even in paradise. The others reflect quietly, and a calm, classically dressed woman at right rests her hand on a shepherd's shoulder. This is a second, more meditative version of a subject Poussin had painted more dramatically a decade earlier (now at Chatsworth). The figures are arranged like a classical relief, and the mood is serene, philosophical acceptance of mortality. Louis XIV bought it in 1685.
creator: poussin

title: Charles I at the Hunt
note: The king as a casually elegant gentleman rather than in armour or robes.
image_file: Portrait de Charles 1er, roi d'Angleterre, à la chasse - Antoon van Dyck - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 1236 ; MR 666.jpg
description: In this portrait of around 1635, Van Dyck shows King Charles I not in armour or royal robes but as a gentleman out hunting. He has dismounted and stands casually with his hand on a cane, looking down at the viewer with an air of effortless superiority. A groom and a page attend his horse, which bows its head as if paying homage. The relaxed pose conceals Charles's short stature and conveys his belief in his natural, divine right to rule. The painting later entered the French royal collection and is now in the Louvre.
creator: van-dyck

title: Marriage A-la-Mode
note: A satirical series on a disastrous arranged marriage between money and rank.
image_file: Marriage A-la-Mode 1, The Marriage Settlement - William Hogarth.jpg
description: This series of six paintings of around 1743, in the National Gallery, London, was engraved and sold to the public in 1745. It tells the story of an arranged marriage between the son of the bankrupt, gout-ridden Earl Squanderfield and the daughter of a rich, miserly city merchant, a deal trading money for rank. The couple are bored and unfaithful from the start. The young viscount catches syphilis, and his wife takes the lawyer Silvertongue as her lover. In the end, the husband is killed by the lawyer in a duel, the lawyer is hanged, and the countess poisons herself while her father pulls the ring from her finger. Every scene is crammed with satirical detail about fashion, art collecting, quack medicine and moral decay.
creator: hogarth

title: The Stonemason's Yard
note: An everyday Venetian scene rather than a tourist view, often considered his finest work.
image_file: Canaletto - The Stonemason's Yard.jpg
description: Painted around 1725, early in his career, this view in the National Gallery, London, shows not a famous monument but the everyday Campo San Vidal in Venice, temporarily turned into a stonemasons' workshop. In the foreground, masons dress blocks of stone for the rebuilding of the church of San Vidal. A mother rushes to a toddler who has fallen, women gossip at a window, and laundry hangs from a balcony. Across the Grand Canal, sunlit, rises the church and bell tower of Santa Maria della Carità. The warm light, the strong shadows and the sense of real working life make it one of Canaletto's finest paintings.
creator: canaletto

title: Würzburg Residence staircase ceiling
note: Apollo and allegories of the four continents on one of the largest ceiling frescoes ever painted.
image_file: Tiepolo, Giovanni - Deckenfresko im Treppenhaus der Würzburger Residenz - Detail Amerika.jpg
description: Between 1752 and 1753, Tiepolo painted the vault over the grand staircase of the Würzburg Residence, the palace of the Prince-Bishop Karl Philipp von Greiffenclau. The vault was designed by the architect Balthasar Neumann and is one of the largest ceiling frescoes ever painted, around 600 square metres. As visitors climb the stairs, the ceiling unfolds: at the centre, the sun god Apollo rises in a radiant sky, and around the cornice are allegories of the four known continents, Europe, Asia, Africa and America, each crowded with people, animals and exotic costumes. In the Europe section Tiepolo included portraits of the prince-bishop, of Neumann sitting on a cannon with his dog, and of himself and his son Giandomenico. The vault survived the bombing of Würzburg in 1945.
creator: tiepolo

title: The Ray
note: A gutted skate hangs above a kitchen table; it won him entry to the French Academy.
image_file: La Raie - Jean Baptiste Siméon Chardin - Musée du Louvre Peintures INV 3197.jpg
description: This large still life of 1728, in the Louvre, helped win Chardin admission to the Royal Academy. In a kitchen, a gutted skate (ray) hangs from a hook, its pale belly forming an eerie, almost human face, its red insides glistening. Beside it, a cat with bristling fur steps over a pile of oysters, eyeing the food. A knife sticks out from the table edge, and pots, a jug and a cloth complete the scene. Chardin's thick, tactile paint makes each texture palpable. Later artists including Cézanne, Matisse and Soutine studied and copied it.
creator: chardin

title: Madame de Pompadour
note: The king's mistress and Boucher's patron, surrounded by books and roses.
image_file: Boucher Marquise de Pompadour -1756.jpg
description: Boucher painted this full-length portrait of Jeanne-Antoinette Poisson, Marquise de Pompadour, mistress of Louis XV, in 1756. She reclines on a sofa in a magnificent sea-green silk gown trimmed with pink ribbons and roses. Around her are signs of her intellectual and artistic patronage: books, a writing desk with letters and a quill, engravings and a mirror reflecting a bookcase. Her little spaniel lies at her feet. The portrait presents her as an enlightened patron of the arts and letters rather than just a royal favourite. It is in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich.
creator: boucher

title: Mr and Mrs Andrews
note: A young landowning couple beside a wide view of their Suffolk estate.
image_file: Thomas Gainsborough - Mr and Mrs Andrews.jpg
description: Gainsborough painted this double portrait around 1750, soon after the wedding of Robert Andrews and Frances Carter in 1748, at their estate, Auberies, near Sudbury. The couple are posed at the left under an oak tree, he standing with his gun and dog, she seated in a blue silk dress. Most of the canvas is given to a wide view of their well-kept fields, with sheaves of corn, sheep and distant woods, a proud display of land ownership and modern agriculture. An unfinished area on Mrs Andrews's lap may have been meant for a book, a bird, or perhaps a future child. The National Gallery bought it in 1960.
creator: gainsborough

title: The Nightmare
note: A demon crouches on a sleeping woman; it caused a sensation at the Royal Academy.
image_file: Johann Heinrich Füssli - The Nightmare 55.5.A-d1-2019-04-15.jpg
description: Fuseli's sensational painting of 1781, shown at the Royal Academy in 1782, made him famous overnight. A young woman in white lies sprawled across a bed, her head and arms hanging backwards in a deep, troubled sleep. On her chest squats a demonic incubus, and a wild-eyed horse, a pun on 'mare', thrusts its head through the curtains. The picture fused eroticism, horror and dream at a time of growing interest in the irrational. Engravings spread it widely, it was parodied in caricatures, and Fuseli painted several versions. This first version is in the Detroit Institute of Arts.
creator: fuseli

title: The Ancient of Days
location: Copies in several collections, incl. the British Museum
note: The frontispiece of 'Europe a Prophecy': a creator figure measures the world with a compass.
image_file: Europe a Prophecy copy K plate 01.jpg
description: This image is the frontispiece to Blake's illuminated book Europe a Prophecy (1794). Within a blazing circle, an old man with streaming white hair and beard crouches and reaches down into the darkness with a great golden compass to measure out the universe. It refers to a passage in the Book of Proverbs about God setting a compass on the face of the deep. In Blake's own mythology the figure is Urizen, the embodiment of reason and law, a creator but also a limiting tyrant. Blake printed it in relief and coloured it by hand. According to his friend Frederick Tatham, he was colouring a copy shortly before his death. Copies are in the British Museum, the Whitworth in Manchester and elsewhere.
creator: blake

title: The Horse Fair
location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: Her largest work, based on visits to the Paris horse market, for which she obtained police permission to wear trousers.
image_file: Rosa Bonheur, The Horse Fair, 1852–55.jpg
description: Bonheur spent around 18 months attending the horse market on the boulevard de l'Hôpital in Paris, near the Salpêtrière hospital, dressed in men's clothing to avoid attention. This huge canvas, about 5 metres wide, was first shown at the 1853 Salon and reworked over the next two years. It shows grooms struggling to control powerful Percheron horses as they are paraded and sold, in a whirl of movement and dust. Bonheur is said to have included herself among the riders. The painting toured Britain, where Queen Victoria saw it in a private viewing, and it was bought by the American railroad magnate Cornelius Vanderbilt, who gave it to the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1887.
creator: bonheur

title: Ophelia
note: Shakespeare's Ophelia floating in a stream, with every plant painted from life.
image_file: John Everett Millais - Ophelia - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted in 1851–52 and now in Tate Britain, this painting illustrates the death of Ophelia in Shakespeare's Hamlet: after her father's death and Hamlet's rejection, she falls into a stream and drowns while singing. Millais spent months painting the riverbank background on the spot beside the Hogsmill River in Surrey, recording every plant in meticulous detail, many with symbolic meaning: the poppy for death, violets for faithfulness, daisies for innocence. The model was Elizabeth Siddal, who posed in a bath of water in his London studio. The lamps under the bath went out, she caught a severe cold, and her father demanded that Millais pay the doctor's bills.
creator: millais

title: Proserpine
note: Proserpine holds the pomegranate that binds her to the underworld; modelled by Jane Morris.
image_file: Dante Gabriel Rossetti - Proserpine - Google Art Project.jpg
description: In Roman myth, Proserpine (Persephone) was abducted by Pluto, god of the underworld. She was allowed to return to her mother, Ceres, only for part of each year, because she had eaten a few pomegranate seeds in the underworld. Rossetti shows her in a dim palace corridor, holding the bitten pomegranate, a sliver of daylight from the world above falling on the wall behind her. An incense burner and a trailing ivy branch, a symbol of clinging memory, are beside her, and Rossetti's own sonnet on the subject is inscribed in Italian on a scroll at top right. The model was Jane Morris, the wife of William Morris and Rossetti's great love, herself trapped in an unhappy marriage. Rossetti painted at least eight versions. This one, of 1874, is in Tate Britain.
creator: rossetti

title: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1 (Whistler's Mother)
note: Titled as a formal study, it became an American icon of motherhood.
image_file: Whistlers Mother high res.jpg
description: Whistler painted his mother, Anna McNeill Whistler, in his London studio in 1871. She had stepped in when another model failed to appear and sat in profile because she was too tired to stand. Seated against a grey wall in a black dress and white lace cap, she is part of a carefully balanced composition of rectangles: a curtain with a Japanese-style pattern, a framed print on the wall and the footstool. Whistler insisted that the title expressed its true subject, an arrangement of colours and forms. The Royal Academy nearly rejected it. In 1891 the French state bought it, and in the 20th century it became an American icon of motherhood, even appearing on a US postage stamp. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: whistler

title: Madame X (Madame Pierre Gautreau)
location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
note: Its daring pose caused a scandal at the 1884 Salon and prompted Sargent's move to London.
image_file: Madame X (Madame Pierre Gautreau), John Singer Sargent, 1884 (unfree frame crop).jpg
description: Virginie Amélie Avegno Gautreau was an American-born Parisian society beauty, married to a French banker, known for her lavender-powdered skin and striking profile. Sargent persuaded her to sit for him and painted her in 1883–84 in a daringly low-cut black satin gown with jewelled straps, her head in sharp profile and her body turned towards us. At the Salon of 1884, the pose and the original right strap, painted slipping off her shoulder, caused a scandal. Sargent repainted the strap, and he moved to London soon afterwards. He kept the painting for more than 30 years and sold it in 1916 to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, calling it the best thing he had ever done. The anonymous title was meant to protect the sitter's identity.
creator: sargent

title: Boulevard Montmartre at Night
note: His only night scene in a series of views from a hotel window.
image_file: Camille Pissarro - Boulevard Montmartre at Night - c 1897 - National Gallery UK.jpg
description: In 1897 Pissarro rented a room in the Grand Hôtel de Russie in Paris overlooking the busy Boulevard Montmartre. From its window he painted a series of views of the boulevard in different weather and at different times of day. This is the only night scene in the series. Wet pavements reflect the yellowish glow of the shop windows and the newly installed electric street lights, while carriages and pedestrians become flickering dabs of paint. It is one of the first great paintings of a city at night. It is in the National Gallery, London.
creator: pissarro

title: The Child's Bath
note: A high viewpoint and flat patterns show the influence of Japanese prints.
image_file: Mary Cassatt - The Child's Bath - Google Art Project.jpg
description: In this painting of 1893, in the Art Institute of Chicago, a mother in a striped dress sits holding her small child on her lap and washing the child's feet in a basin. Both look down at the water, absorbed. Cassatt's high viewpoint, flat patterns on the carpet, wallpaper and dress, and strong outlines owe much to the Japanese prints she had seen in Paris in 1890. The scene is intimate and ordinary but monumental in its composition, and it is one of Cassatt's best-known works.
creator: cassatt

title: The Floor Scrapers
note: Urban labourers shown frankly; the Salon rejected it as vulgar.
image_file: Gustave Caillebotte - The Floor Planers - Google Art Project.jpg
description: In this painting of 1875, three shirtless workmen kneel on the floor of an elegant, empty Parisian apartment, scraping the wooden floorboards to prepare them for varnishing. Light from the window and balcony behind them falls across their backs and arms and glistens on the scraped strips of wood, while curls of shavings pile up around them. A wine bottle and glass stand nearby. The Salon jury rejected it in 1875, probably because it showed urban labourers so frankly and without moral message. Caillebotte showed it at the second Impressionist exhibition in 1876. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: caillebotte

title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
note: Umbrella-carrying Parisians on a new boulevard, with photographic cropping.
image_file: Gustave Caillebotte - Paris Street; Rainy Day - Google Art Project.jpg
description: This large painting, shown at the third Impressionist exhibition in 1877 and now in the Art Institute of Chicago, depicts an intersection in the new Paris quartier de l'Europe, near the Gare Saint-Lazare. Elegantly dressed pedestrians carry umbrellas across the wet, shiny cobblestones, while Haussmann's uniform cream-coloured apartment buildings recede in a steep perspective. A green lamp post divides the composition in two. A fashionable couple walks towards us at the right, and their figures are sharply cut off by the picture's edge, almost like a photograph. The painting captures the modern experience of the city: anonymous, orderly and isolating.
creator: caillebotte

title: The Sleeping Gypsy
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: A lion sniffs a sleeping wanderer under a moonlit desert sky.
image_file: La Bohémienne endormie.jpg
description: In this painting of 1897, a mandolin player in a striped robe lies asleep on a desert under a full moon, a water jug beside her. A lion approaches and sniffs at her, but seems not to attack. The scene is utterly still and mysterious, painted in Rousseau's smooth, flat style with crisp outlines and pale colours. Rousseau offered it to the town council of his home town, Laval, which turned it down. It disappeared for years, was rediscovered in 1923 and acclaimed by the Surrealists for its dreamlike quality. It is in the Museum of Modern Art, New York.
creator: rousseau

title: At the Moulin Rouge
note: Cabaret regulars, with the artist himself in the background and an eerie green-lit face at the right.
image_file: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, At the Moulin Rouge.jpg
description: Painted in 1892–95, this painting in the Art Institute of Chicago shows a group of regulars at the Moulin Rouge dance hall in Montmartre. A group of men and women sit around a table drinking. In the background the dancer La Goulue arranges her hair in front of a mirror, and Toulouse-Lautrec himself walks past with his much taller cousin, Gabriel Tapié de Céleyran. At the right edge, a woman's face is cut off by the frame and lit in a ghostly green by the gaslight. The strange angle and lighting give the scene an unsettling, almost sinister mood.
creator: toulouse-lautrec

title: Self-Portrait with Physalis
note: A tense, twisting self-image with a sprig of red Chinese lantern fruit.
image_file: Egon Schiele - Self-Portrait with Physalis - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted in 1912, the year of Schiele's brief imprisonment, this self-portrait in the Leopold Museum in Vienna shows the artist's head and shoulders, turning sharply. His head tilts towards his shoulder and he looks out at the viewer with a fixed, intense gaze. Beside him are a sprig of physalis (Chinese lantern plant) with red fruits and a few leaves, set against a bare white background. The sharp outlines, flat white space and twisted pose create tension. It was painted as a companion to his portrait of Wally Neuzil, which is the same size.
creator: schiele

title: Street, Dresden
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: Mask-like faces in acid pink and orange convey urban alienation.
image_file: Kirchner - Street, Dresden, 1908, 12.1951.jpg
description: Kirchner painted this street scene in Dresden in 1908 and reworked it in 1919. Fashionably dressed women and other figures crowd the pavement in strident, unnatural colours of pink, orange and green, and their mask-like faces stare blankly. The pavement tilts upward, and a tram is visible in the background. The sense of crowding and isolation, the tension and the lurid colour express the anxiety of the modern city. It anticipates his famous Berlin street scenes of 1913–15. It is in the Museum of Modern Art, New York.
creator: kirchner

title: The Large Blue Horses
note: Blue stood for spirituality and the masculine in Marc's colour symbolism.
image_file: Franz Marc - Die großen blauen Pferde 1911.jpg
description: In this painting of 1911, the year he co-founded the Blue Rider, three massive blue horses are packed tightly together, their bodies curving and overlapping in rhythmic arcs, set against rolling red and yellow hills and green and red trees. For Marc, blue symbolised the masculine and spiritual, and horses embodied a pure, innocent relationship with nature that humans had lost. The painting's harmony of bold colour and curving form makes it one of the icons of German Expressionism. It is in the Walker Art Center in Minneapolis.
creator: marc

title: Twittering Machine
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: Wiry birds on a crank-driven perch: a whimsical image with a dark edge.
image_file: Die Zwitscher-Maschine (Twittering Machine), 1922 - Paul Klee.jpg
description: In this small work of 1922, made with Klee's oil-transfer drawing technique and watercolour, four birdlike creatures with spindly legs perch on a thin wire or branch connected to a hand crank, beaks open. If the crank were turned, they would presumably twitter. Against a misty pinkish-blue background, the image is both whimsical and slightly sinister: the birds may be lures, and below them is a pit. It has been read as a satire on mechanised society and the mechanisation of nature and art. In 1937 the Nazis confiscated it from the National Gallery in Berlin as 'degenerate', and in 1939 the Museum of Modern Art in New York acquired it.
creator: klee

title: Nu couché (Reclining Nude)
note: From a series of nudes whose 1917 exhibition was shut down by the police on opening day.
image_file: Modigliani - Nu couché.jpg
description: Painted in 1917–18, this large painting belongs to the series of reclining nudes that Modigliani made for his dealer Léopold Zborowski. Some of these nudes caused the police to close his only solo exhibition in 1917. A woman with a pale, elongated face and closed eyes lies across the whole width of the canvas, her warm, glowing body set against dark red and blue drapery. It draws on the tradition of Giorgione, Titian, Ingres and Manet, but with a frank, modern sensuality. In 2015 it sold at auction for $170.4 million to the Chinese collector Liu Yiqian, one of the highest prices ever paid for a painting at auction.
creator: modigliani

title: Unique Forms of Continuity in Space
location: Casts at MoMA, New York; Tate; Museo del Novecento, Milan
note: A striding figure streamlined by speed; it appears on the Italian 20-cent euro coin.
image_file: 'Unique Forms of Continuity in Space', 1913 bronze by Umberto Boccioni.jpg
description: Boccioni modelled this striding figure in plaster in 1913, his most famous sculpture and the key work of Futurism. It shows a human body in motion, its muscles stretched and swept back as if shaped by the speed and the air around it, so that the figure merges with its own movement. Boccioni wanted to show not a body at a single moment but the continuous flow of its motion. The plaster original is in São Paulo. The bronze casts in New York, London and Milan were made after his death, in 1931 and later. The sculpture appears on the reverse of the Italian 20-cent euro coin.
creator: boccioni

title: Black Square
note: Hung in the corner like an icon at the 0.10 exhibition in Petrograd: a 'zero point' of painting.
image_file: Kazimir Malevich, 1915, Black Suprematic Square, oil on linen canvas, 79.5 x 79.5 cm, Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.jpg
description: Malevich first exhibited this painting, a black square on a white ground, at the Last Futurist Exhibition of Paintings 0,10 in Petrograd in December 1915. It hung high in the corner of the room, the place where an icon traditionally hangs in Russian homes. He presented it as the 'zero point' of painting, the beginning of Suprematism, an art of pure feeling free from depicting objects. The paint of the original has cracked badly. In 2015 researchers at the Tretyakov Gallery found two earlier colourful compositions underneath and a handwritten inscription referring to an old joke picture by the French humorist Alphonse Allais. Malevich painted three later versions.
creator: malevich

title: Bird in Space
location: Versions at MoMA (1928 bronze), the Met, Philadelphia Museum of Art, Seattle Art Museum and others
note: A US customs case in 1928 ruled that it was art, not taxable metal.
description: Brâncuși began the theme of the bird around 1910 with Maiastra, a magic bird from Romanian folklore. In 1923 he made the first Bird in Space, and he went on to make around 16 versions in marble and polished bronze. The bird's wings and feathers are eliminated, leaving a slender, tapering form that rises from a narrow foot and seems to soar, the essence of flight rather than an image of a bird. When a version was shipped to the United States in 1926, customs officials refused to classify it as art and taxed it as a manufactured metal object. In 1928 a court ruled in Brâncuși's favour, a landmark decision for modern art. Versions are in the Museum of Modern Art, the Metropolitan Museum, the Philadelphia Museum of Art and elsewhere.
creator: brancusi

title: Jimson Weed/White Flower No. 1
location: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, Bentonville
note: In 2014 it set the record for a painting by a woman artist at auction.
description: O'Keeffe painted this canvas in 1932. It shows a single white jimson weed (datura) blossom, a flower that grows around her home in New Mexico and opens at dusk. She enlarged the flower to fill the canvas, so that its petals become an almost abstract form against a soft blue-grey and green background. She said she painted flowers big so that busy people would take time to see them. In 2014 it sold at auction for $44.4 million, a record for a work by a woman artist at the time, and it went to the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville, Arkansas.
creator: okeeffe

title: American Gothic
note: A farmer and his daughter before a house with a Gothic window; one of the most parodied images in American art.
image_file: Grant Wood - American Gothic (1930).jpg
description: In 1930 Grant Wood saw a small white house in Eldon, Iowa, with a Gothic Revival window in the gable, and imagined the kind of people who might live there. He painted a stern farmer holding a pitchfork and a woman beside him in front of the house. The models were his sister, Nan Wood Graham, and his dentist, Byron McKeeby. Wood said they were meant to be a father and his daughter, not husband and wife. The pitchfork's three tines are echoed in the stitching of the man's overalls and the window. The painting won a prize at the Art Institute of Chicago in 1930, which bought it. It quickly became an icon of rural America and one of the most parodied images in art. Whether it satirises small-town Midwestern values or celebrates them is still debated.
creator: grant-wood

title: Woman I
location: Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), New York
note: A ferocious female figure built and rebuilt over two years of reworking.
description: De Kooning worked on Woman I from 1950 to 1952, painting, scraping and repainting it dozens of times. At one point he abandoned it, and the art historian Meyer Schapiro reportedly encouraged him to continue. The result is a ferocious female figure with huge staring eyes, a toothy grin and massive breasts, built up from slashing, violent brushstrokes of pink, yellow, green and blue that merge with the background. Drawing on ancient fertility figures and American billboard pin-ups, it shocked critics who saw abstraction as the only serious path. It has been criticised as misogynistic and praised as a powerful image. The Museum of Modern Art acquired it in 1953.
creator: de-kooning

title: Untitled (Skull)
note: A head part X-ray, part mask, from his first year as a painter.
description: Basquiat painted this large canvas, about 2 metres high, in 1981, early in his career. It was shown at his first solo gallery exhibition in New York in 1982 and bought that year by the collectors Eli and Edythe Broad. A huge head fills the canvas: part skull, part mask, part anatomical diagram, with gaping eyes, a mouth full of teeth and a brain area filled with lines, colours and patterns. It seems at once alive and dead, revealing both the outside and the inside of the head. It has been read as a self-portrait and as an allusion to African masks and the history of Black identity. It is in The Broad in Los Angeles.
creator: basquiat

title: Vitruvian Man
note: A study of ideal proportions after the Roman architect Vitruvius; rarely shown because of its fragility.
image_file: Da Vinci Vitruve Luc Viatour.jpg
description: This pen-and-ink drawing of about 1490 illustrates a passage by the Roman architect Vitruvius, who said that a well-proportioned human body fits into both a circle and a square. Leonardo drew a nude man with two overlapping positions of arms and legs. Standing with arms outstretched, he fits the square. Spread-eagled, his navel becomes the centre of the circle. Leonardo's mirror-written notes around the drawing record the body's proportions. The image has become a universal symbol of science, harmony and the Renaissance belief that man is the measure of all things. It belongs to the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice and is exhibited only rarely because it is so fragile.
creator: leonardo

title: The Supper at Emmaus
note: The disciples recognise the risen Christ; the fruit basket seems to tip out of the picture.
image_file: 1602-3 Caravaggio,Supper at Emmaus National Gallery, London.jpg
description: In Luke's Gospel, two disciples meet a stranger on the road to Emmaus after the Crucifixion and recognise him as the risen Christ only when he blesses bread at supper. Caravaggio painted the instant of recognition in 1601, for the Roman nobleman Ciriaco Mattei. One disciple starts to rise from his chair, the other flings his arms wide, and his outstretched hand seems to pierce the picture plane. The innkeeper looks on, puzzled. Christ is shown young and beardless, which is unusual. A basket of fruit perches precariously on the very edge of the table, about to fall into our space. It is in the National Gallery, London.
creator: caravaggio

title: Portrait of Innocent X
note: A piercing papal portrait that obsessed Francis Bacon centuries later.
image_file: Retrato del Papa Inocencio X. Roma, by Diego Velázquez.jpg
description: Velázquez painted Pope Innocent X during his second visit to Rome in 1650. The elderly pope sits in a red armchair against a red curtain, his red cap and cape set against white lace. He fixes the viewer with a suspicious, shrewd glare. The brushwork is wonderfully loose, especially in the shimmering silks. According to tradition, the pope remarked that it was 'too true'. The portrait remains in the Doria Pamphilj family's gallery in Rome. In the 20th century it obsessed Francis Bacon, who painted dozens of 'screaming popes' based on it without ever seeing the original.
creator: velazquez

title: The Art of Painting
note: An allegory of painting seen past a heavy curtain; Vermeer kept it until his death.
image_file: Jan Vermeer - The Art of Painting - Google Art Project.jpg
description: In this painting of around 1666–68, in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, a heavy tapestry curtain is pulled back to reveal a painter, seen from behind in a fine slashed doublet, at work. His model is dressed as Clio, the Muse of history, with a laurel wreath, a trumpet and a book. On the wall hangs a large map of the Seventeen Provinces of the Netherlands, with a crease that some see as dividing the Dutch Republic from the Spanish Netherlands. An elaborate chandelier displays the double-headed Habsburg eagle. Vermeer seems to have valued the painting greatly: after his death his widow tried to keep it from his creditors. Adolf Hitler bought it in 1940, and after the war it went to the Vienna museum. A restitution claim by heirs of the former owners was rejected by an Austrian advisory board in 2011.
creator: vermeer

title: Self-Portrait with Two Circles
note: A late self-portrait with palette and brushes before two mysterious arcs.
image_file: Rembrandt Self-portrait (Kenwood).jpg
description: Painted in the last years of his life, around 1665–69, this self-portrait shows Rembrandt standing in his working clothes and a white cap, holding his palette, brushes and maulstick. He looks out at us with a steady gaze. Behind him on the wall are two mysterious partial circles. They have been interpreted as references to world maps, to symbols of perfection and theory, or to the legend of the ancient painter Apelles drawing a perfect circle freehand. The face is built up with thick, energetic paint, while the hands are barely sketched. It is in Kenwood House in London.
creator: rembrandt

title: The Slave Ship
note: Based on a real atrocity in which enslaved people were thrown overboard during a storm.
image_file: Slave-ship.jpg
description: Turner exhibited this painting in 1840 with the title Slavers Throwing Overboard the Dead and Dying – Typhoon Coming On. It was inspired by accounts of the Zong massacre of 1781, when the crew of a British slave ship threw more than 130 enslaved Africans overboard to claim insurance. In the foreground, shackled legs and arms sink into a sea of blood-red and gold, surrounded by fish and gulls. The ship sails away into a furious storm and sunset. It was shown at a time of continuing campaigns against slavery worldwide. The critic John Ruskin owned it for many years. It is now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
creator: turner

title: Woman with a Parasol – Madame Monet and Her Son
location: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C.
note: Camille and Jean on a breezy hillside, seen from below against a bright sky.
image_file: Claude Monet - Woman with a Parasol - Madame Monet and Her Son - Google Art Project.jpg
description: Painted in 1875 at Argenteuil, this painting in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, shows Monet's wife Camille and their seven-year-old son Jean on a hillside on a breezy summer day. Seen from below against a bright blue sky with white clouds, Camille holds a green parasol, and her white dress and veil flutter in the wind. Painted with rapid, fluid strokes, it captures a fleeting moment of light and movement rather than a formal portrait. Monet returned to the theme in 1886 with two paintings of a woman with a parasol, now in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: monet

title: L'Absinthe
note: Two isolated drinkers in a Paris café; scandalous when shown in London in 1893.
image_file: Edgar Degas - In a Café - Google Art Project 2.jpg
description: Painted in 1875–76, this scene of café life was posed by Degas's friends, the actress Ellen Andrée and the painter Marcellin Desboutin, at the Café de la Nouvelle Athènes in Montmartre, where the Impressionists met. A woman sits slumped and vacant-eyed in front of a glass of cloudy green absinthe beside a pipe-smoking man who looks away from her. The zigzag arrangement of the empty tables and the off-centre composition reinforce the mood of isolation. When it was shown in London in 1893, critics attacked it as a degrading lesson in drunkenness. It is in the Musée d'Orsay.
creator: degas

title: The Card Players
location: Versions at Musée d'Orsay, the Met, the Courtauld, the Barnes and a private collection
note: Provençal peasants absorbed in a game; one version sold privately for a record price in 2011.
image_file: Les Joueurs de cartes, par Paul Cézanne.jpg
description: In the early 1890s Cézanne painted a series of five paintings of Provençal peasants playing cards. Some of them were workers on his family's estate, the Jas de Bouffan near Aix. The larger versions, in the Barnes Foundation and the Metropolitan Museum, show four or five figures. The three smaller versions, in the Musée d'Orsay, the Courtauld and a private collection, show just two men facing each other across a table, absorbed in the game. The figures are solid and still, like monuments. One version was sold privately around 2011, reportedly for more than $250 million, among the highest prices ever paid for a work of art.
creator: cezanne

title: Wheatfield with Crows
note: A turbulent sky over a wheatfield, painted in Auvers in his last weeks.
image_file: Korenveld met kraaien - s0149V1962 - Van Gogh Museum.jpg
description: Van Gogh painted this canvas in July 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, in the last weeks of his life. Its unusual double-square format stretches out a field of wheat under a dark, stormy blue sky, with a flock of black crows flying low over the corn. Three paths lead into the field and seem to go nowhere. In a letter he described painting vast fields of wheat under troubled skies and trying to express sadness and extreme loneliness, but also the healthy and strengthening power of the countryside. Despite the legend, it was probably not his last painting. It is in the Van Gogh Museum, Amsterdam.
creator: van-gogh
